name: playbooks/test-mongodb8-upgrade.yml
review_question: Is this Ansible artifact excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Testweise MongoDB-8-Upgrade-Vorbereitung
     3: #
     4: # Phase 1 (jetzt): mongodump vom laufenden Live-System, Restore in temporären
     5: # MongoDB-8-Container auf tools1. Das Live-System (RocketChat + MongoDB 7)
     6: # bleibt vollständig unberührt.
     7: #
     8: # Bitnami-Legacy-Images werden nicht mehr gepflegt; das Upgrade wechselt zu
     9: # mongodb/mongodb-community-server (offizielles Image). Datenpfad ändert sich:
    10: # /bitnami/mongodb  →  /data/db
    11: #
    12: # Phase 2 (später ergänzen): RocketChat stoppen → dump → neues Volume mit
    13: # MongoDB 8 → restore → RocketChat mit neuer Version starten.
    14: #
    15: # Voraussetzungen:
    16: #   - Playbook läuft auf tools1.hamburg.adfc.de
    17: #   - Live-Container docker-rocket-mongodb-1 läuft
    18: #   - Freier Speicher auf / (Dump-Datei landet in /usr/local/share/rocketchat/)
    19: 
    20: - name: MongoDB 8 Upgrade – Testweise Datenübernahme
    21:   hosts: tools1.hamburg.adfc.de
    22:   gather_facts: false
    23: 
    24:   vars:
    25:     test_dir: /usr/local/share/rocketchat/mongo8-upgrade-test
    26:     dump_file: "{{ test_dir }}/mongodump.gz"
    27:     test_container: mongodb8-upgrade-test
    28:     test_volume: mongodb8-upgrade-test-data
    29:     mongodb8_image: mongodb/mongodb-community-server:8.0-ubi8
    30:     live_container: docker-rocket-mongodb-1
    31: 
    32:   tasks:
    33:     - name: Testverzeichnis anlegen
    34:       ansible.builtin.file:
    35:         path: "{{ test_dir }}"
    36:         state: directory
    37:         mode: "0700"
    38:         owner: root
    39:         group: root
    40: 
    41:     - name: Speicherplatz auf / prüfen
    42:       ansible.builtin.command:
    43:         argv:
    44:           - df
    45:           - -BM
    46:           - --output=avail
    47:           - /
    48:       register: df_out
    49:       changed_when: false
    50: 
    51:     - name: Speicherplatz ausgeben
    52:       ansible.builtin.debug:
    53:         msg: "Freier Speicherplatz auf /: {{ df_out.stdout_lines[-1] | trim | replace('M', '') }} MB"
    54: 
    55:     - name: Abbruch wenn weniger als 2 GB frei
    56:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    57:         msg: "Zu wenig Speicherplatz: {{ df_out.stdout_lines[-1] | trim | replace('M', '') }} MB frei, mindestens 2048 MB benötigt"
    58:       when: (df_out.stdout_lines[-1] | trim | replace('M', '') | int) < 2048
    59: 
    60:     # --- mongodump vom laufenden Live-Container ---
    61: 
    62:     - name: mongodump vom Live-Container erstellen (Live-System bleibt in Betrieb)
    63:       ansible.builtin.shell:
    64:         cmd: >
    65:           docker exec {{ live_container }}
    66:           sh -c 'mongodump --archive --gzip'
    67:           > {{ dump_file }}
    68:           2> {{ test_dir }}/mongodump.log
    69:         executable: /bin/bash
    70:       register: dump_result
    71: 
    72:     - name: Dump-Log ausgeben
    73:       ansible.builtin.command:
    74:         argv:
    75:           - tail
    76:           - "-5"
    77:           - "{{ test_dir }}/mongodump.log"
    78:       changed_when: false
    79:       register: dump_log
    80: 
    81:     - name: Dump-Log anzeigen
    82:       ansible.builtin.debug:
    83:         msg: "{{ dump_log.stdout_lines }}"
    84: 
    85:     - name: Dump-Dateigröße prüfen
    86:       ansible.builtin.stat:
    87:         path: "{{ dump_file }}"
    88:       register: dump_stat
    89: 
    90:     - name: Abbruch wenn Dump leer ist
    91:       ansible.builtin.fail:
    92:         msg: "Dump-Datei ist leer oder fehlt: {{ dump_file }}"
    93:       when: not dump_stat.stat.exists or dump_stat.stat.size < 1024
    94: 
    95:     - name: Dump-Größe ausgeben
    96:       ansible.builtin.debug:
    97:         msg: "Dump-Größe: {{ (dump_stat.stat.size / 1024 / 1024) | round(1) }} MB"
    98: 
    99:     # --- Alten Test-Container und -Volume aufräumen ---
   100: 
   101:     - name: Prüfen ob Test-Container bereits existiert
   102:       ansible.builtin.command:
   103:         argv:
   104:           - docker
   105:           - ps
   106:           - -aq
   107:           - --filter
   108:           - "name=^/{{ test_container }}$"
   109:       register: existing_container
   110:       changed_when: false
   111: 
   112:     - name: Alten Test-Container entfernen
   113:       ansible.builtin.command:
   114:         argv:
   115:           - docker
   116:           - rm
   117:           - -f
   118:           - "{{ test_container }}"
   119:       when: existing_container.stdout | trim != ""
   120: 
   121:     - name: Prüfen ob Test-Volume bereits existiert
   122:       ansible.builtin.command:
   123:         argv:
   124:           - docker
   125:           - volume
   126:           - ls
   127:           - -q
   128:           - --filter
   129:           - "name={{ test_volume }}"
   130:       register: existing_volume
   131:       changed_when: false
   132: 
   133:     - name: Altes Test-Volume entfernen
   134:       ansible.builtin.command:
   135:         argv:
   136:           - docker
   137:           - volume
   138:           - rm
   139:           - "{{ test_volume }}"
   140:       when: existing_volume.stdout | trim != ""
   141: 
   142:     # --- MongoDB 8 Test-Container starten ---
   143: 
   144:     - name: MongoDB-8-Image pullen
   145:       ansible.builtin.command:
   146:         argv:
   147:           - docker
   148:           - pull
   149:           - "{{ mongodb8_image }}"
   150:       register: pull_result
   151:       changed_when: "'Pull complete' in pull_result.stdout or 'Downloaded newer' in pull_result.stdout"
   152: 
   153:     - name: MongoDB-8-Test-Container starten
   154:       ansible.builtin.command:
   155:         argv:
   156:           - docker
   157:           - run
   158:           - -d
   159:           - --name
   160:           - "{{ test_container }}"
   161:           - --volume
   162:           - "{{ test_volume }}:/data/db"
   163:           - "{{ mongodb8_image }}"
   164:           - --replSet
   165:           - rs0
   166:           - --bind_ip_all
   167: 
   168:     - name: Warten bis MongoDB 8 bereit ist (max. 60 s)
   169:       ansible.builtin.command:
   170:         argv:
   171:           - docker
   172:           - exec
   173:           - "{{ test_container }}"
   174:           - mongosh
   175:           - --quiet
   176:           - --eval
   177:           - db.runCommand({ping:1}).ok
   178:       register: mongo_ping
   179:       retries: 12
   180:       delay: 5
   181:       until: mongo_ping.stdout | trim == "1"
   182:       changed_when: false
   183: 
   184:     - name: Replica Set rs0 initialisieren
   185:       ansible.builtin.command:
   186:         argv:
   187:           - docker
   188:           - exec
   189:           - "{{ test_container }}"
   190:           - mongosh
   191:           - --quiet
   192:           - --eval
   193:           - 'rs.initiate({_id:"rs0",members:[{_id:0,host:"localhost:27017"}]})'
   194:       register: rs_init
   195: 
   196:     - name: Warten bis Test-Container PRIMARY ist (max. 30 s)
   197:       ansible.builtin.command:
   198:         argv:
   199:           - docker
   200:           - exec
   201:           - "{{ test_container }}"
   202:           - mongosh
   203:           - --quiet
   204:           - --eval
   205:           - rs.status().myState
   206:       register: rs_state
   207:       retries: 10
   208:       delay: 3
   209:       until: rs_state.stdout | trim == "1"
   210:       changed_when: false
   211: 
   212:     # --- Daten wiederherstellen ---
   213: 
   214:     - name: mongorestore in Test-Container (local.* wird übersprungen)
   215:       ansible.builtin.shell:
   216:         cmd: >
   217:           cat {{ dump_file }} |
   218:           docker exec -i {{ test_container }}
   219:           mongorestore
   220:           --archive
   221:           --gzip
   222:           --drop
   223:           --nsExclude='local.*'
   224:           2>&1
   225:         executable: /bin/bash
   226:       register: restore_result
   227: 
   228:     - name: Restore-Ausgabe anzeigen
   229:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   230:         msg: "{{ restore_result.stdout_lines[-10:] }}"
   231: 
   232:     # --- Ergebnis prüfen ---
   233: 
   234:     - name: Benutzeranzahl in rocketchat.users prüfen
   235:       ansible.builtin.command:
   236:         argv:
   237:           - docker
   238:           - exec
   239:           - "{{ test_container }}"
   240:           - mongosh
   241:           - rocketchat
   242:           - --quiet
   243:           - --eval
   244:           - db.users.countDocuments()
   245:       register: user_count
   246:       changed_when: false
   247: 
   248:     - name: Räume-Anzahl in rocketchat.rocketchats prüfen
   249:       ansible.builtin.command:
   250:         argv:
   251:           - docker
   252:           - exec
   253:           - "{{ test_container }}"
   254:           - mongosh
   255:           - rocketchat
   256:           - --quiet
   257:           - --eval
   258:           - db.rocketchats.countDocuments()
   259:       register: room_count
   260:       changed_when: false
   261: 
   262:     - name: Ergebnis-Zusammenfassung ausgeben
   263:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   264:         msg:
   265:           - "✓ Datenbank erfolgreich in MongoDB 8 importiert"
   266:           - "  Benutzer:  {{ user_count.stdout | trim }}"
   267:           - "  Räume:     {{ room_count.stdout | trim }}"

   269:           - "Test-Container läuft noch für manuelle Inspektion:"

   271:           - ""

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Purpose: Update one existing VLAN's mutable properties (name, mtu, space,
     3: # primary_rack, dhcp_on, relay_vlan). Called once per (fabric, vlan) pair from the loop
     4: # in networking.yml AFTER subnets and IP ranges exist — MAAS rejects
     5: # dhcp_on=true on a VLAN with no dynamic range, which is why this is split
     6: # from vlan_create.yml.
     7: #
     8: # Expects:
     9: #   - _fname / pair.0.fabric           : fabric name (the loop variable
    10: #                                        normalizes whichever is set)
    11: #   - vlan / pair.1                    : the desired VLAN dict from
    12: #                                        `maas_networking[*].vlans[*]`
    13: #   - _fabric_by_name                  : { "<fabric_name>": <fabric_id> }
    14: #   - _vlan_index                      : { "<fabric_name>": { "<vid_str>":
    15: #                                        <vlan_obj> } } from vlan_build_index
    16: #   - _maas_api, maas_auth_header
    17: #   - _global_primary_rack_controller  : optional; per-VLAN
    18: #                                        `vlan.primary_rack_controller`
    19: #                                        wins when set, otherwise we fall
    20: #                                        back to this global value.
    21: # Returns: nothing.
    22: # Side effects: PUT {{ _maas_api }}/fabrics/<fid>/vlans/<vid>/ with the
    23: # computed update body.
    24: 
    25: - name: Normalize inputs
    26:   set_fact:
    27:     _fname: "{{ _fname | default(pair.0.fabric) }}"
    28:     _fid: "{{ _fabric_by_name[pair.0.fabric] }}"
    29:     vlan:  "{{ vlan  | default(pair.1) }}"
    30: 
    31: - name: Ensure VLAN present in index
    32:   assert:
    33:     that:
    34:       - _vlan_index[_fname] is defined
    35:       - _vlan_index[_fname][vlan.vid | string] is defined
    36:     fail_msg: >-
    37:       VLAN {{ vlan.vid }} not found in index for fabric {{ _fname }}.
    38:       Known vids: {{ _vlan_index.get(_fname, {}) | dict2items | map(attribute='key') | list }}
    39: 
    40: - name: Clear any stale per-VLAN variables
    41:   set_fact:
    42:     _vlan_id: "{{ none }}"
    43:     _vobj: "{{ none }}"
    44:     _prc_candidate: ""
    45:     _primary_rack_controller: "{{ none }}"
    46:     _relay_requested: false
    47:     _relay_vid: ""
    48:     _relay_vlan_id: ""
    49: 
    50: - name: Resolve VLAN object
    51:   set_fact:
    52:     _vobj: "{{ _vlan_index[_fname][vlan.vid | string] }}"
    53: 
    54: - name: And ID
    55:   set_fact:
    56:     _vlan_id: "{{ _vobj.id | string }}"
    57: 
    58: # Set the Primary Rack Controller to the VLAN-level defined one.  Otherwise empty string.
    59: - name: Compute per-VLAN primary rack controller candidate
    60:   set_fact:
    61:     _prc_candidate: "{{ (vlan | default({})).get('primary_rack_controller') | default('', true) | string | trim }}"
    62: 
    63: # Use the VLAN-level defined PRC discovered above or use the global one.
    64: - name: Decide primary rack controller for this VLAN
    65:   set_fact:
    66:     _primary_rack_controller: "{{ _prc_candidate if (_prc_candidate | length) > 0 else (_global_primary_rack_controller | default(omit)) }}"
    67: 
    68: # --- DHCP relay ---------------------------------------------------------------
    69: # `relay_vlan: <vid>` on a VLAN tells MAAS that DHCP/PXE traffic for this VLAN
    70: # arrives relayed on another VLAN of the same fabric, so MAAS stops "fixing"
    71: # things by moving the subnet to the VLAN the traffic was seen on. The MAAS API
    72: # wants the target VLAN's database id, not its vid, so resolve it through
    73: # _vlan_index (which holds every VLAN MAAS knows about on the fabric, not just
    74: # the ones defined in maas_networking). `relay_vlan: ''` (or null) explicitly
    75: # clears an existing relay; omitting the key leaves MAAS untouched.
    76: - name: Compute requested relay target
    77:   set_fact:
    78:     _relay_requested: "{{ 'relay_vlan' in vlan }}"
    79:     _relay_vid: "{{ vlan.relay_vlan | default('', true) | string | trim }}"
    80: 
    81: - name: Ensure relay target VLAN exists on the fabric
    82:   assert:
    83:     that:
    84:       - _vlan_index[_fname][_relay_vid] is defined
    85:     fail_msg: >-
    86:       relay_vlan {{ _relay_vid }} on {{ _fname }}:{{ vlan.vid }} does not match
    87:       any VLAN MAAS knows about on fabric {{ _fname }}.
    88:       Known vids: {{ _vlan_index.get(_fname, {}) | dict2items | map(attribute='key') | list }}
    89:   when:
    90:     - _relay_requested | bool
    91:     - _relay_vid | length > 0
    92: 
    93: - name: Resolve relay target VLAN database id
    94:   set_fact:
    95:     _relay_vlan_id: "{{ _vlan_index[_fname][_relay_vid].id | string }}"
    96:   when:
    97:     - _relay_requested | bool
    98:     - _relay_vid | length > 0
    99: 
   100: - name: Build VLAN update body
   101:   vars:
   102:     _spaces_list: >-
   103:       {{
   104:         (vlan.subnets | default([]))
   105:         | selectattr('space','defined')
   106:         | map(attribute='space') | list | unique
   107:       }}
   108:     _desired_space: "{{ _spaces_list[0] if (_spaces_list | length) == 1 else omit }}"
   109: 
   110:     _has_dynamic_for_vlan: >-
   111:       {{
   112:         (vlan.subnets | default([]))
   113:         | selectattr('ip_ranges','defined')
   114:         | map(attribute='ip_ranges') | flatten
   115:         | selectattr('type','equalto','dynamic')
   116:         | list | length > 0
   117:       }}
   118:   set_fact:
   119:     _vlan_update_body: >-
   120:       {{
   121:         {'name': vlan.name}
   122:         | combine( (vlan.mtu is defined) | ternary({'mtu': vlan.mtu}, {}), recursive=True )
   123:         | combine( (_desired_space is not none) | ternary({'space': _desired_space}, {}), recursive=True )
   124:         | combine(
   125:             (vlan.dhcp_on | default(false) | bool and (_primary_rack_controller is defined))
   126:             | ternary({'primary_rack': _primary_rack_controller}, {}), recursive=True
   127:           )
   128:         | combine(
   129:             (vlan.dhcp_on | default(false) | bool and _has_dynamic_for_vlan)
   130:             | ternary({'dhcp_on': true}, {}), recursive=True
   131:           )
   132:         | combine(
   133:             (_relay_requested | bool)
   134:             | ternary({'relay_vlan': (_relay_vlan_id if (_relay_vid | length > 0) else '')}, {}), recursive=True
   135:           )
   136:       }}
   137: 
   138: - include_tasks: ../_auth_header.yml
   139:   no_log: true
   140: 
   141: - name: Update VLAN properties
   142:   uri:
   143:     url: "{{ _maas_api }}/fabrics/{{ _fid }}/vlans/{{ vlan.vid }}/"
   144:     method: PUT
   145:     headers:
   146:       Authorization: "{{ maas_auth_header }}"
   147:       Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
   148:       Accept: application/json
   149:     body_format: form-urlencoded
   150:     body: "{{ _vlan_update_body }}"
   151:     status_code: [200]
   152:     return_content: true
   153:     use_netrc: false
   154:   no_log: true

1: ---
     2: # Mint a long-lived Vikunja API token for each MCP service user and publish the
     3: # shared connection (URL + per-tier tokens) to OpenBao secret/ai/mcp/vikunja.
     4: #
     5: # Mirrors ansible-splunk roles/splunk_docker/tasks/manage_one_user.yml:
     6: #   * mint only when absent (idempotent — Vikunja returns the key exactly once)
     7: #   * sibling-preserving KV-v2 read-modify-write
     8: #   * no_log on every secret-bearing task
     9: # Included from tasks/main.yml only when vikunja_token_publish_openbao is true.
    10: # The converge enables it with -e '{"vikunja_token_publish_openbao": true}';
    11: # BAO_ADDR/BAO_TOKEN must be in the CONTROLLER environment.
    12: #
    13: # Permissions are built from the LIVE GET /api/v1/routes response, never
    14: # hardcoded: Vikunja's PermissionsAreValid rejects any group/action not in the
    15: # current route set, and the route-group keys are derived from URL paths (so
    16: # they shift across versions). Building from the running instance keeps the
    17: # minted permissions valid by construction.
    18: 
    19: - name: Assert OpenBao write credentials are present
    20:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    21:     that:
    22:       - vikunja_token_openbao_addr | length > 0
    23:       - vikunja_token_openbao_token | length > 0
    24:     fail_msg: >-
    25:       vikunja_token_publish_openbao is on but BAO_ADDR/BAO_TOKEN are unset.
    26:       Provide a write-capable OpenBao AppRole in the converge environment.
    27:     quiet: true
    28: 
    29: - name: Log in to Vikunja as admin to read the token route catalogue
    30:   ansible.builtin.uri:
    31:     url: "http://localhost:{{ vikunja_port }}/api/v1/login"
    32:     method: POST
    33:     body_format: json
    34:     body:
    35:       username: "{{ vikunja_admin_user }}"
    36:       password: "{{ vikunja_admin_password }}"
    37:     status_code: [200]
    38:   register: vikunja_admin_login
    39:   no_log: true
    40: 
    41: - name: Fetch the API token route catalogue
    42:   ansible.builtin.uri:
    43:     url: "http://localhost:{{ vikunja_port }}/api/v1/routes"
    44:     method: GET
    45:     headers:
    46:       Authorization: "Bearer {{ vikunja_admin_login.json.token }}"
    47:     status_code: [200]
    48:   register: vikunja_routes
    49:   no_log: true
    50: 
    51: - name: Determine in-scope Vikunja route groups
    52:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    53:     vikunja_scoped_groups: "{{ vikunja_mcp_token_scopes | select('in', vikunja_routes.json) | list }}"
    54: 
    55: # read_all/read_one are the only read actions; create/update/delete are writes.
    56: # RW grants every action on a scoped group; RO grants only the read_* actions,
    57: # dropping any group left with none.
    58: - name: Build read-write and read-only permission maps
    59:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    60:     vikunja_rw_permissions: >-
    61:       {{ dict(vikunja_scoped_groups
    62:               | zip(vikunja_scoped_groups | map('extract', vikunja_routes.json) | map('list'))) }}
    63:     vikunja_ro_permissions: >-
    64:       {{ dict(vikunja_scoped_groups
    65:               | zip(vikunja_scoped_groups | map('extract', vikunja_routes.json)
    66:                     | map('list') | map('select', 'match', 'read') | map('list')))
    67:          | dict2items | rejectattr('value', 'eq', []) | items2dict }}
    68: 
    69: - name: Assert MCP token permission scopes resolved
    70:   ansible.builtin.assert:
    71:     that:
    72:       - vikunja_rw_permissions | length > 0
    73:       - vikunja_ro_permissions | length > 0
    74:     fail_msg: >-
    75:       No Vikunja route groups matched vikunja_mcp_token_scopes
    76:       ({{ vikunja_mcp_token_scopes | join(', ') }}) in GET /api/v1/routes.
    77:     quiet: true
    78: 
    79: - name: Mint and publish MCP tokens per service user
    80:   ansible.builtin.include_tasks: mcp_token_one.yml
    81:   loop: "{{ vikunja_mcp_token_users }}"
    82:   loop_control:
    83:     loop_var: vikunja_mcp_user
    84:     label: "{{ vikunja_mcp_user.username }}"

1: ---
     2: # Homarr via the community-scripts install layer, pinned and offline-sourced.
     3: #
     4: # Order matters: every helper the installer sources must be on disk BEFORE the
     5: # base URL is rewritten, and the base URL must be rewritten BEFORE the installer
     6: # runs. Otherwise the "pinned" install quietly reaches the internet for three of
     7: # its four helpers.
     8: 
     9: # =============================================================================
    10: # 0. Supply what the borrowed installer assumes it already has
    11: # =============================================================================
    12: 
    13: - name: Install the prerequisites the borrowed installer does not install itself
    14:   # Measured: without gnupg the install dies at `setup_nodejs` with rc=250 and
    15:   # the misleading message "Failed to import NodeSource GPG key" — the key
    16:   # downloads fine, but `gpg --dearmor` is missing. `file` is used by the same
    17:   # helper to auto-detect the key format.
    18:   #
    19:   # These are normally seeded by `build.func` when upstream creates the
    20:   # container itself. Borrowing only the install/ half means the caller owns
    21:   # that seeding — one more thing the community layer does not hand over.
    22:   ansible.builtin.apt:
    23:     name:
    24:       - ca-certificates
    25:       - curl
    26:       - file
    27:       - gnupg
    28:       - jq
    29:       - sudo
    30:       - tar
    31:     state: present
    32:     update_cache: true
    33:     cache_valid_time: 3600
    34: 
    35: # =============================================================================
    36: # 1-2. Fetch the pinned artifacts
    37: # =============================================================================
    38: 
    39: - name: Create the pinned community-scripts directory
    40:   ansible.builtin.file:
    41:     path: "{{ homarr_cs_pinned_dir }}/{{ item }}"
    42:     state: directory
    43:     owner: root
    44:     group: root
    45:     mode: "0755"
    46:   loop:
    47:     - misc
    48:     - install
    49: 
    50: - name: Fetch the pinned community-scripts artifacts used verbatim
    51:   # `checksum:` is the load-bearing part, not the tag in the URL. get_url fails
    52:   # the task on a mismatch, so a moved tag stops the converge instead of
    53:   # installing something nobody reviewed.
    54:   ansible.builtin.get_url:
    55:     url: "{{ homarr_cs_upstream_base }}/{{ item.path }}"
    56:     dest: "{{ homarr_cs_pinned_dir }}/{{ item.path }}"
    57:     checksum: "sha256:{{ item.sha256 }}"
    58:     owner: root
    59:     group: root
    60:     mode: "0644"
    61:   loop: "{{ homarr_cs_artifacts }}"
    62:   loop_control:
    63:     label: "{{ item.path }}"
    64: 
    65: - name: Fetch the pinned artifacts that need patching, unmodified
    66:   ansible.builtin.get_url:
    67:     url: "{{ homarr_cs_upstream_base }}/{{ item.path }}"
    68:     dest: "{{ homarr_cs_pinned_dir }}/{{ item.path }}.upstream"
    69:     checksum: "sha256:{{ item.sha256 }}"
    70:     owner: root
    71:     group: root
    72:     mode: "0644"
    73:   loop: "{{ homarr_cs_patched_artifacts }}"
    74:   loop_control:
    75:     label: "{{ item.path }}"
    76: 
    77: # =============================================================================
    78: # 3-4. Derive the working helpers: no upstream reads, no interactive preflight
    79: # =============================================================================
    80: 
    81: - name: Assert the endpoints the borrowed installer actually needs are reachable
    82:   # This is the check, and it must come before the patch below removes
    83:   # upstream's own preflight. Something has to assert connectivity, or the
    84:   # install fails deep inside a half-finished apt transaction instead of here.
    85:   #
    86:   # These are what the installer genuinely depends on: the GitHub API and
    87:   # release CDN, which `fetch_and_deploy_gh_release` uses to resolve and pull
    88:   # the Homarr build. Note it resolves "latest" — pinning this role's tag does
    89:   # not pin what lands here. That is recorded in the ADR, not hidden.
    90:   #
    91:   # The question is REACHABILITY, so any HTTP status answers it — a status code
    92:   # of any kind proves DNS, TCP and TLS all worked. A real connectivity failure
    93:   # surfaces as a timeout or a transport error instead.
    94:   #
    95:   # Hence the deliberately wide list. 404: the release CDN has no root document.
    96:   # 403/429: the GitHub API rate-limits unauthenticated callers at 60/hour, and
    97:   # a repeated test run exhausts that — treating it as unreachable would fail
    98:   # the install for the one reason that says nothing about the network.
    99:   ansible.builtin.uri:
   100:     url: "{{ item }}"
   101:     method: HEAD
   102:     status_code: [200, 301, 302, 403, 404, 429]
   103:     timeout: 15
   104:   loop:
   105:     - https://api.github.com/
   106:     - https://objects.githubusercontent.com/
   107:   changed_when: false
   108: 
   109: - name: Read the unmodified upstream helpers
   110:   ansible.builtin.slurp:
   111:     src: "{{ homarr_cs_pinned_dir }}/{{ item.path }}.upstream"
   112:   loop: "{{ homarr_cs_patched_artifacts }}"
   113:   loop_control:
   114:     label: "{{ item.path }}"
   115:   register: homarr_cs_upstream_content
   116: 
   117: - name: Write the patched helpers
   118:   # Two substitutions, both load-bearing:
   119:   #
   120:   # 1. Every `.../ProxmoxVE/main/...` read becomes a `file://` read of the
   121:   #    pinned copies. That covers install.func's `_FUNC_BASE` bootstrap of
   122:   #    core.func + error_handler.func, its tools.func pull inside update_os,
   123:   #    and core.func's cosmetic header fetch. curl reads file:// URLs, so the
   124:   #    helpers load unchanged apart from where they come from. It also rewrites
   125:   #    the `/usr/bin/update` line customize() writes into a path we
   126:   #    deliberately never populate, so the unpinned self-updater cannot work
   127:   #    even if task 7 were skipped.
   128:   #
   129:   # 2. `network_check()` returns immediately. Measured: left in place, the
   130:   #    install exits 122 in under two seconds. It pings 1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8 /
   131:   #    9.9.9.9 and, when both IPv4 and IPv6 fail, prompts with
   132:   #    `read ... </dev/tty`. Under Ansible there is no controlling terminal, so
   133:   #    the read errors, the empty answer counts as "no", and it exits. Neither
   134:   #    half survives contact with this estate: the firewall is default-deny, so
   135:   #    an app-VLAN guest has no reason to ping public resolvers, and no
   136:   #    converge ever has a TTY. This is not routing around a failing check —
   137:   #    the task above replaces it with the reachability that actually matters,
   138:   #    over the protocol the installer really uses. The pattern only appears in
   139:   #    install.func; applying it to core.func is a no-op.
   140:   ansible.builtin.copy:
   141:     dest: "{{ homarr_cs_pinned_dir }}/{{ item.item.path }}"
   142:     content: >-
   143:       {{ (item.content | b64decode)
   144:          | regex_replace('https://raw\.githubusercontent\.com/community-scripts/ProxmoxVE/main',
   145:                          'file://' ~ homarr_cs_pinned_dir)
   146:          | regex_replace('(?m)^network_check\(\) \{$',
   147:                          "network_check() {\n  return 0 # neutralised by ansible-proxmox-apps (role: homarr)") }}
   148:     owner: root
   149:     group: root
   150:     mode: "0644"
   151:   loop: "{{ homarr_cs_upstream_content.results }}"
   152:   loop_control:
   153:     label: "{{ item.item.path }}"
   154: 
   155: # =============================================================================
   156: # 4b. Make redis startable in an unprivileged LXC, before the installer needs it
   157: # =============================================================================
   158: 
   159: - name: Ensure the redis-server drop-in directory exists
   160:   ansible.builtin.file:
   161:     path: /etc/systemd/system/redis-server.service.d
   162:     state: directory
   163:     owner: root
   164:     group: root
   165:     mode: "0755"
   166: 
   167: - name: Allow redis to start without nested user namespacing
   168:   # Measured on the live guest, and NOT catchable by the molecule scenario:
   169:   # Debian 13's redis-server.service sets `PrivateUsers=true`, which needs a
   170:   # nested user namespace. Inside an unprivileged LXC without the `nesting`
   171:   # feature that is denied, so the unit dies with 217/USER and the borrowed
   172:   # installer aborts at `systemctl enable -q --now redis-server`.
   173:   #
   174:   # Upstream never hits this because build.func creates its containers with
   175:   # nesting enabled. Ours derives nesting only from the `docker` tag
   176:   # (modules/proxmox-container/locals.tf), and `features` is in the container's
   177:   # ignore_changes, so it is effectively set-once at creation.
   178:   #
   179:   # Disabling PrivateUsers for this one unit is the narrower change. The
   180:   # alternative — turning on container-wide `nesting` — grants nested
   181:   # namespacing to everything in the guest to fix one service. The container is
   182:   # already unprivileged and user-namespaced by the host (uid 0 maps to 100000),
   183:   # so what is lost here is a second, inner namespace around redis, not the
   184:   # isolation boundary that matters.
   185:   ansible.builtin.copy:
   186:     dest: /etc/systemd/system/redis-server.service.d/10-lxc-privateusers.conf
   187:     owner: root
   188:     group: root
   189:     mode: "0644"
   190:     content: |
   191:       # Managed by ansible-proxmox-apps (role: homarr).
   192:       # PrivateUsers requires a nested user namespace, which an unprivileged
   193:       # LXC without the nesting feature cannot provide (systemd 217/USER).
   194:       [Service]
   195:       PrivateUsers=false
   196:   notify: Reload systemd and clear failed units
   197: 
   198: - name: Apply the drop-in before the installer enables redis
   199:   ansible.builtin.meta: flush_handlers
   200: 
   201: # =============================================================================
   202: # 5. Run the borrowed installer, exactly once
   203: # =============================================================================
   204: 
   205: - name: Install Homarr via the pinned community-scripts installer
   206:   # FUNCTIONS_FILE_PATH carries the CONTENT of install.func, not a path — the
   207:   # install script does `source /dev/stdin <<<"$FUNCTIONS_FILE_PATH"`. That
   208:   # env-var indirection is the only reason this path can be pinned at all; the
   209:   # ct/ scripts hardcode a URL instead.
   210:   #
   211:   # PASSWORD is set non-empty on purpose. The installer's customize() adds a
   212:   # root autologin override to the container console when it is empty, which is
   213:   # not something we want on a guest whose access model is the SSH CA.
   214:   #
   215:   # DIAGNOSTICS=no suppresses upstream's telemetry ping.
   216:   ansible.builtin.shell:
   217:     cmd: >-
   218:       set -o pipefail;
   219:       export FUNCTIONS_FILE_PATH="$(cat {{ homarr_cs_pinned_dir }}/misc/install.func)";
   220:       bash {{ homarr_cs_pinned_dir }}/install/homarr-install.sh
   221:     creates: "{{ homarr_installed_marker }}"
   222:   environment:
   223:     # Everything below is part of the contract build.func would normally have
   224:     # exported before calling the install script. Borrowing only the install/
   225:     # half means reproducing that contract by hand, and the helpers run under
   226:     # `set -u`, so a missing one aborts mid-install rather than degrading.
   227:     #
   228:     # APPLICATION is the display name motd_ssh() writes into the login banner;
   229:     # unset, the install dies at install.func line 492.
   230:     # `app` is what customize() interpolates into /usr/bin/update. That updater
   231:     # is replaced immediately after, but the variable still has to exist.
   232:     APPLICATION: Homarr
   233:     app: homarr
   234:     # SSH_ROOT=no is a security decision, not a default. With "yes", motd_ssh()
   235:     # rewrites sshd_config to PermitRootLogin yes and restarts sshd — which
   236:     # would quietly undo the SSH CA access model on this guest.
   237:     SSH_ROOT: "no"
   238:     # Empty, but it must EXIST. customize() guards on `[[ -n "${SSH_AUTHORIZED_KEY}" ]]`,
   239:     # and under `set -u` that test itself aborts when the variable is unset —
   240:     # the guard does not protect you, it is the thing that fails. Keys on this
   241:     # guest come from the SSH CA, so the value stays empty.
   242:     SSH_AUTHORIZED_KEY: ""
   243:     # PASSWORD non-empty keeps customize() from adding a root autologin getty
   244:     # to the container console.
   245:     PASSWORD: managed-by-ansible
   246:     DIAGNOSTICS: "no"
   247:     tz: "{{ ansible_date_time.tz | default('UTC') }}"
   248:     DEBIAN_FRONTEND: noninteractive
   249:   args:
   250:     executable: /bin/bash
   251:   timeout: "{{ homarr_install_timeout }}"
   252:   # No changed_when: `creates` already reports unchanged when it short-circuits
   253:   # and changed when it actually runs, which is exactly the desired semantics.
   254:   # A hand-written changed_when here only got it wrong.
   255: 
   256: - name: Stamp the install as complete
   257:   # Only reachable when the task above exited 0, because a non-zero exit fails
   258:   # the play. That is what makes this a trustworthy `creates:` guard.
   259:   ansible.builtin.file:
   260:     path: "{{ homarr_installed_marker }}"
   261:     state: touch
   262:     owner: root
   263:     group: root
   264:     mode: "0644"
   265:     modification_time: preserve
   266:     access_time: preserve
   267: 
   268: # =============================================================================
   269: # 6-7. Take ownership back from the installer
   270: # =============================================================================
   271: 
   272: - name: Replace the installer's unpinned self-updater
   273:   # customize() writes /usr/bin/update as a curl|bash of the ct/ script on the
   274:   # `main` branch. Leaving it in place would hand any root shell a one-word way
   275:   # to pull and execute unreviewed code, and to move the app version outside
   276:   # any change record. Ansible owns updates here.
   277:   ansible.builtin.copy:
   278:     dest: /usr/bin/update
   279:     owner: root
   280:     group: root
   281:     mode: "0755"
   282:     content: |
   283:       #!/usr/bin/env bash
   284:       echo "Managed by ansible-proxmox-apps (role: homarr)." >&2
   285:       echo "Bump homarr_cs_tag, re-checksum, review the diff, then converge." >&2
   286:       exit 1
   287: 
   288: - name: Ensure Homarr and redis are enabled and running
   289:   ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
   290:     name: "{{ item }}"
   291:     state: started
   292:     enabled: true
   293:     daemon_reload: true
   294:   loop:
   295:     - redis-server
   296:     - "{{ homarr_service_name }}"
   297: 
   298: # =============================================================================
   299: # 8. Prove it actually serves
   300: # =============================================================================
   301: 
   302: - name: Wait for the Homarr port to accept connections
   303:   ansible.builtin.wait_for:
   304:     host: 127.0.0.1
   305:     port: "{{ homarr_port }}"
   306:     timeout: 180
   307: 
   308: - name: Verify Homarr answers over HTTP
   309:   ansible.builtin.uri:
   310:     url: "http://127.0.0.1:{{ homarr_port }}/"
   311:     method: GET
   312:     status_code: [200, 302, 307]
   313:   register: homarr_health
   314:   retries: 10
   315:   delay: 6
   316:   until: homarr_health.status in [200, 302, 307]
   317:   changed_when: false
   318: 
   319: # Everything above installs the app. Everything below configures it — the part
   320: # no installer emits, and the reason borrowing the install step does not shrink
   321: # a role by much.
   322: - name: Own the runtime environment file
   323:   ansible.builtin.include_tasks: configure.yml
   324: 
   325: - name: Build the shared service catalog
   326:   ansible.builtin.include_role:
   327:     name: dashboard_catalog
   328: 
   329: - name: Converge the API key, integrations, and board tiles
   330:   ansible.builtin.include_tasks: integrations.yml

     2: # =============================================================================
     3: # Phase 0: APT Cache Infrastructure
     4: # apt-cacher-ng must be deployed BEFORE any roles that install apt packages
     5: # =============================================================================
     6: 
     7: - name: Deploy apt-cacher-ng caching proxy
     8:   hosts: apt_cacher_group
     9:   become: true
    10:   gather_facts: true
    11:   tags:
    12:     - apt_cacher_ng
    13:     - apt_proxy
    14:     - lxc
    15:   roles:
    16:     - role: apt_cacher_ng
    17: 
    18: - name: Configure apt proxy on LXC containers
    19:   hosts: lxc_containers:!apt_cacher_group:!download_vpn_group
    20:   become: true
    21:   gather_facts: false
    22:   tags:
    23:     - apt_proxy
    24:     - lxc
    25:   tasks:
    26:     # The cache is an HA pair (tofu node_services generates one instance per
    27:     # always-on node; all carry the `apt-cache` tag, so apt_cacher_group tracks
    28:     # them with no inventory change here). apt itself supports only a single
    29:     # Acquire::http::Proxy value, so instance selection uses apt's native
    30:     # Proxy-Auto-Detect hook instead: at every apt run the script probes each
    31:     # instance by FQDN and prints the first live one, or DIRECT so apt fails
    32:     # open when the whole pool is down. An instance (or its node) going down
    33:     # therefore costs one probe timeout, never apt itself.
    34:     - name: Deploy apt proxy autodetect script
    35:       when: groups['apt_cacher_group'] | default([]) | length > 0
    36:       vars:
    37:         _apt_cache_port: >-
    38:           {{ tofu_data.constants.service_ports.apt_cacher_ng
    39:              | default(3142) }}
    40:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    41:         dest: /usr/local/bin/apt-proxy-detect
    42:         content: |
    43:           #!/bin/bash
    44:           # Managed by Ansible (ansible-proxmox-apps site.yml) — do not edit.
    45:           # apt Acquire::http::Proxy-Auto-Detect hook: first live cache wins,
    46:           # DIRECT when none answer (fail open, apt fetches upstream).
    47:           for host in {% for h in groups['apt_cacher_group'] | sort -%}
    48:           {{ h }}.{{ tofu_data.domain }} {% endfor %}; do
    49:             if timeout 2 bash -c "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/${host}/{{ _apt_cache_port }}" 2>/dev/null; then
    50:               exec 3>&- 2>/dev/null
    51:               echo "http://${host}:{{ _apt_cache_port }}"
    52:               exit 0
    53:             fi
    54:           done
    55:           echo DIRECT
    56:         owner: root
    57:         group: root
    58:         mode: '0755'
    59: 
    60:     - name: Configure apt proxy
    61:       when: groups['apt_cacher_group'] | default([]) | length > 0
    62:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    63:         dest: /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/00proxy
    64:         content: |
    65:           Acquire::http::Proxy-Auto-Detect "/usr/local/bin/apt-proxy-detect";
    66:         owner: root
    67:         group: root
    68:         mode: '0644'
    69: 
    70:     - name: Remove stale apt proxy configuration
    71:       when: groups['apt_cacher_group'] | default([]) | length == 0
    72:       ansible.builtin.file:
    73:         path: "{{ item }}"
    74:         state: absent
    75:       loop:
    76:         - /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/00proxy

    79: 
    80: # =============================================================================
    81: # Phase 0-zot: Zot OCI Registry
    82: # Self-hosted pull-through cache (docker.io/ghcr.io/quay.io) and private
    83: # registry. Deployed early — before any docker app roles — so firewalled
    84: # docker hosts can pull through it. Pairs with the tofu registry LXC 109.

   139: # =============================================================================
   140: # Phase 0a: NTP Time Synchronization Baseline

     9: # real docker host over SSH is what makes this playbook AAP-runnable

    16: # arches map (see their `when: netboot_arches_resolved is not defined`

    18: #
    19: # Idempotency: a SHA256 of the rendered user_overrides plus the resolved
    20: # git SHA of the cloned netboot.xyz repo is recorded in MANIFEST.lastbuild
    21: # after each successful run. On re-run, if the hash matches AND every
    22: # expected output binary exists, the container build is skipped. The
    23: # MANIFEST lives on the builder host and persists across runs.

    73:   ansible.builtin.file:
    74:     path: "{{ _netboot_build_dir }}/output"
    75:     state: directory
    76:     mode: "0755"
    77: 
    78: - name: Clone or update netboot.xyz source at the pinned ref
    79:   ansible.builtin.git:
    80:     repo: "{{ netboot_xyz_repo }}"
    81:     dest: "{{ _netboot_build_dir }}/src"
    82:     version: "{{ netboot_xyz_ref }}"
    83:     force: true
    84:   environment:

    86:     # (e.g., `insteadOf = https://github.com/`). The clone is anonymous
    87:     # HTTPS against a public repo, so no creds are needed.
    88:     GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: /dev/null

    92:   ansible.builtin.template:
    93:     src: "{{ playbook_dir }}/templates/netboot/user_overrides.yml.j2"
    94:     dest: "{{ _netboot_build_dir }}/src/user_overrides.yml"
    95:     mode: "0644"
    96:   register: _netboot_template

    98: - name: Read the rendered user_overrides back for hashing

   100:   # rendered file lives on the builder, so slurp it back rather than
   101:   # using lookup('file') (which only reads the controller filesystem).
   102:   ansible.builtin.slurp:
   103:     src: "{{ _netboot_build_dir }}/src/user_overrides.yml"
   104:   register: _netboot_overrides_slurp

   106: - name: Compute a build-input hash (rendered overrides + git SHA)
   107:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   108:     _netboot_build_hash: >-
   109:       {{
   110:         ((_netboot_overrides_slurp.content | b64decode)
   111:          ~ _netboot_git.after) | hash('sha256')
   112:       }}
   113: 
   114: - name: Read prior build hash if present
   115:   ansible.builtin.slurp:
   116:     src: "{{ _netboot_build_dir }}/MANIFEST.lastbuild"
   117:   register: _netboot_lastbuild
   118:   failed_when: false
   119:   changed_when: false
   120: 
   121: - name: Stat each expected output binary
   122:   ansible.builtin.stat:
   123:     path: "{{ _netboot_build_dir }}/output/ipxe/{{ item.local_name }}"
   124:   loop: "{{ netboot_arches_resolved }}"
   125:   loop_control:
   126:     label: "{{ item.public_name }}"
   127:   register: _netboot_output_stat
   128: 
   129: - name: Decide whether to invoke the builder container
   130:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   131:     _netboot_need_build: >-
   132:       {{
   133:         (_netboot_lastbuild.content | default('') | b64decode | trim)
   134:           != _netboot_build_hash
   135:         or
   136:         (_netboot_output_stat.results
   137:           | rejectattr('stat.exists', 'equalto', true) | list | length) > 0
   138:       }}
   139: 
   140: - name: Run the netboot.xyz builder container  # noqa: command-instead-of-module
   141:   # netboot_container_runtime defaults to docker (the builder host is a
   142:   # real docker host). docker accepts --pull=always and ignores the :Z
   143:   # SELinux relabel suffix on non-SELinux hosts, so the same command
   144:   # works whether the runtime is docker or podman.
   145:   ansible.builtin.command:
   146:     cmd: >-
   147:       {{ netboot_container_runtime | default('docker') }} run --rm
   148:       --pull=always
   149:       -v {{ _netboot_build_dir }}/src:/ansible:Z
   150:       -v {{ _netboot_build_dir }}/output:/var/www/html:Z
   151:       --workdir /ansible
   152:       {{ netboot_builder_image }}
   153:       ansible-playbook site.yml
   154:   when: _netboot_need_build
   155:   changed_when: true
   156:   register: _netboot_build_run
   157: 
   158: - name: Re-stat each expected output binary after build
   159:   ansible.builtin.stat:
   160:     path: "{{ _netboot_build_dir }}/output/ipxe/{{ item.local_name }}"
   161:   loop: "{{ netboot_arches_resolved }}"
   162:   loop_control:
   163:     label: "{{ item.public_name }}"
   164:   register: _netboot_output_stat_post
   165: 
   166: - name: Assert all expected binaries exist after build
   167:   ansible.builtin.assert:
   168:     that:
   169:       - item.stat.exists
   170:     fail_msg: >-
   171:       Expected output binary
   172:       {{ _netboot_build_dir }}/output/ipxe/{{ item.item.local_name }}
   173:       is missing after the build step. Check the builder container's
   174:       ansible-playbook output (the prior task) for errors.
   175:   loop: "{{ _netboot_output_stat_post.results }}"
   176:   loop_control:
   177:     label: "{{ item.item.public_name }}"
   178: 
   179: - name: Persist build hash for next run
   180:   ansible.builtin.copy:
   181:     dest: "{{ _netboot_build_dir }}/MANIFEST.lastbuild"
   182:     content: "{{ _netboot_build_hash }}"
   183:     mode: "0644"
   184:   when: _netboot_need_build
   185: 
   186: - name: Write human-readable MANIFEST
   187:   ansible.builtin.copy:
   188:     dest: "{{ _netboot_build_dir }}/MANIFEST"
   189:     mode: "0644"
   190:     content: |
   191:       ref: {{ netboot_xyz_ref }}
   192:       git_sha: {{ _netboot_git.after }}
   193:       built_at: {{ ansible_date_time.iso8601 | default(lookup('pipe', 'date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')) }}
   194:       artifacts:
   195:       {% for item in netboot_arches_resolved %}
   196:         - ipxe/{{ item.local_name }}
   197:       {% endfor %}
   198:   when: _netboot_need_build
   199: 
   200: # Pull the freshly built binaries from the builder back to the
   201: # controller's build cache, where the upload/verify stages (second play,
   202: # against rb5009) expect them. Always fetch: it is cheap (~3 MB total)
   203: # and keeps the controller cache in lockstep with the builder even when
   204: # the container build itself was skipped by the hash gate.
   205: - name: Fetch built binaries from the builder to the controller cache
   206:   ansible.builtin.fetch:
   207:     src: "{{ _netboot_build_dir }}/output/ipxe/{{ item.local_name }}"
   208:     dest: "{{ netboot_local_build_dir }}/output/ipxe/{{ item.local_name }}"
   209:     flat: true
   210:   loop: "{{ netboot_arches_resolved }}"
   211:   loop_control:
   212:     label: "{{ item.public_name }}"

     2: # Apply the david_igou.routeros_configuration.configure role against a device
     3: # using a CAPTURE FILE (.cache/routeros-vars/<host>.yml from export_config.yaml)
     4: # instead of the committed host_vars baseline. This is the graduation harness
     5: # for onboarding a new device or new paths:

    16: #                 igou-inventory/host_vars/<host>.yml and use configure.yaml

    35:     routeros_config_skip_paths: []

name: playbooks/armbian/stage_netboot_assets.yaml
review_question: Is this Ansible artifact excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Per-host netboot staging: netboot server first, then the router.
     3: #   1. boards group: resolve board_config + rootfs_src per host.
     4: #   2. netboot_server group: rootfs_provision role per board host.
     5: #   3. netboot_server group: fetch per-host TFTP artifacts to the
     6: #      controller cache (armbian_tftp_cache_dir).
     7: #   4. boards group (serial): upload kernel/initrd/dtb to the router's
     8: #      flash + register /ip tftp rows, then plumbing-check.
     9: #
    10: # Plays 3-4 replace the collection's stage_router.yml — router staging
    11: # is homelab transport, owned here alongside the rest of transport/.
    12: #
    13: # Scope with -e armbian_boards_group=<group> — not --limit. The plays
    14: # mix boards with netboot_server, and plays 2-3 loop over the boards
    15: # group from the netboot_server host, so --limit silently empties them.
    16: - name: Resolve effective board configs and rootfs sources per board host
    17:   hosts: "{{ armbian_boards_group | default('boards') }}"
    18:   gather_facts: false
    19:   tasks:
    20:     - name: Resolve effective armbian_board_config
    21:       ansible.builtin.include_tasks: tasks/_resolve_board_config.yml
    22:     - name: Resolve armbian_rootfs_src per host
    23:       ansible.builtin.include_tasks: tasks/_resolve_rootfs_src.yml
    24: 
    25: - name: Provision per-host NFS rootfs + TFTP artifacts
    26:   hosts: "{{ armbian_netboot_server_group | default('netboot_server') }}"
    27:   become: true
    28:   gather_facts: false
    29:   tasks:
    30:     - name: Run rootfs_provision per board host
    31:       ansible.builtin.include_role:
    32:         name: david_igou.armbian.rootfs_provision
    33:       vars:
    34:         armbian_rootfs_src: "{{ hostvars[_board].armbian_rootfs_src }}"
    35:         armbian_rootfs_host: "{{ _board }}"
    36:         armbian_rootfs_dtb: "{{ hostvars[_board].armbian_board_config.dtb }}"
    37:         armbian_rootfs_force_refresh: "{{ armbian_force_refresh | default(false) }}"
    38:       loop: "{{ groups[armbian_boards_group | default('boards')] }}"
    39:       loop_control:
    40:         loop_var: _board
    41: 
    42: - name: Fetch per-host TFTP artifacts from netboot server to controller cache
    43:   hosts: "{{ armbian_netboot_server_group | default('netboot_server') }}"
    44:   become: true
    45:   gather_facts: false
    46:   vars:
    47:     _assets: [vmlinuz, initrd.img, board.dtb]
    48:   tasks:
    49:     - name: Ensure controller cache dir exists per host
    50:       ansible.builtin.file:
    51:         path: "{{ armbian_tftp_cache_dir }}/{{ item }}"
    52:         state: directory
    53:         mode: "0755"
    54:       delegate_to: localhost
    55:       # Force a real local connection: inventory `localhost` defaults to
    56:       # SSH (it is an SSH-able build host), and this devcontainer's sshd
    57:       # has PrivateTmp, so an SSH-delegated mkdir creates a private /tmp
    58:       # the fetch below (controller-side write) cannot see.
    59:       vars:
    60:         ansible_connection: local
    61:       become: false
    62:       loop: "{{ groups[armbian_boards_group | default('boards')] }}"
    63: 
    64:     - name: Fetch each (host, asset) pair from netboot server
    65:       ansible.builtin.fetch:
    66:         src: "{{ armbian_image_cache }}/sbc-tftp/{{ item.0 }}/{{ item.1 }}"
    67:         dest: "{{ armbian_tftp_cache_dir }}/{{ item.0 }}/{{ item.1 }}"
    68:         flat: true
    69:       loop: "{{ groups[armbian_boards_group | default('boards')] | product(_assets) | list }}"
    70:       loop_control:
    71:         label: "{{ item.0 }}/{{ item.1 }}"
    72: 
    73: - name: Upload per-host TFTP assets to router and verify plumbing
    74:   hosts: "{{ armbian_boards_group | default('boards') }}"
    75:   gather_facts: false
    76:   # One board at a time: every host's uploads delegate to the same
    77:   # router, and parallel net_put bursts flake RouterOS's SSH server.
    78:   serial: 1
    79:   vars:
    80:     _assets: [vmlinuz, initrd.img, board.dtb]
    81:   tasks:
    82:     - name: Upload TFTP assets to router
    83:       delegate_to: "{{ armbian_router }}"
    84:       block:
    85:         - name: Ensure base armbian dir exists on router flash
    86:           community.routeros.command:
    87:             commands:
    88:               - >-
    89:                 :if ([/file find name="{{ armbian_tftp_flash_dir }}/armbian" type=directory] = "")
    90:                 do={/file add name="{{ armbian_tftp_flash_dir }}/armbian" type=directory}
    91:           register: _basedir
    92:           retries: 3
    93:           delay: 5
    94:           until: _basedir is succeeded
    95:           changed_when: false
    96: 
    97:         - name: Ensure per-host dir exists on router flash
    98:           community.routeros.command:
    99:             commands:
   100:               - >-
   101:                 :if ([/file find name="{{ armbian_tftp_flash_dir }}/armbian/{{ inventory_hostname }}" type=directory] = "")
   102:                 do={/file add name="{{ armbian_tftp_flash_dir }}/armbian/{{ inventory_hostname }}" type=directory}
   103:           register: _hostdir
   104:           retries: 3
   105:           delay: 5
   106:           until: _hostdir is succeeded
   107:           changed_when: false
   108: 
   109:         # Force-remove router-side files so net_put always pushes fresh
   110:         # content — the shared primitive is size-gated, and silently
   111:         # skipping by size has caused stale vmlinuz/rootfs-modules
   112:         # mismatches (router served old kernel; initramfs modprobe
   113:         # failed inside the new rootfs).
   114:         - name: Force-remove router-side assets (stale-content guard)
   115:           community.routeros.command:
   116:             commands:
   117:               - >-
   118:                 /file remove
   119:                 [find name="{{ armbian_tftp_flash_dir }}/armbian/{{ inventory_hostname }}/{{ item }}"]
   120:           register: _preremove
   121:           retries: 3
   122:           delay: 5
   123:           until: _preremove is succeeded
   124:           changed_when: false
   125:           loop: "{{ _assets }}"
   126: 
   127:         - name: Upload each asset via shared primitive
   128:           ansible.builtin.include_tasks: transport/upload_file.yml
   129:           vars:
   130:             _upload_local_src: "{{ armbian_tftp_cache_dir }}/{{ inventory_hostname }}/{{ item }}"
   131:             _upload_remote_path: "{{ armbian_tftp_flash_dir }}/armbian/{{ inventory_hostname }}/{{ item }}"
   132:             _upload_req_filename: "armbian/{{ inventory_hostname }}/{{ item }}"
   133:             _upload_req_filename_is_regex: false
   134:           loop: "{{ _assets }}"
   135: 
   136:         - name: Verify /ip tftp rows landed (plumbing check)
   137:           ansible.builtin.include_tasks: transport/plumbing_check.yml

     2: # Back up RouterOS devices (via david_igou.routeros_configuration.backup) and

    10: # controller.

    12: # NOTE: unlike the pre-collection version of this playbook (which passed
    13: # dont-encrypt=yes), the binary backup is now encrypted by RouterOS with the
    14: # invoking user's password (the SSH user). Restore with
    15: #   /system backup load name=<file> password=<that password>
    16: #
    17: # Uploaded objects are tagged with tier={{ routeros_s3_tier }} (default:
    18: # daily). The rustfs bucket's lifecycle policy keys off this tag. AAP
    19: # schedules routeros_backup_s3_{daily,weekly,monthly} set the tier.
    20: #
    21: # S3 credentials are resolved at runtime from 1Password
    22: # (vault: lab_s3, item: routeros-backups-rustfs-cold,
    23: #  fields: username / password / host).
    24: #
    25: # Default scope: the routeros group. Override target with:
    26: #   -e host=<inventory_hostname>
    27: # Override tier with:
    28: #   -e routeros_s3_tier=<weekly|monthly|...>
    29: - name: Back up RouterOS devices to S3
    30:   hosts: "{{ host | default('routeros') }}"
    31:   gather_facts: false
    32: 
    33:   vars:
    34:     routeros_s3_bucket: routeros-backups
    35:     routeros_s3_prefix: routeros
    36:     routeros_s3_region: us-east-1
    37:     routeros_s3_tier: daily
    38:     routeros_s3_endpoint: "https://{{ lookup('community.general.onepassword', 'routeros-backups-rustfs-cold', field='host', vault='lab_s3') }}"
    39:     routeros_s3_access_key: "{{ lookup('community.general.onepassword', 'routeros-backups-rustfs-cold', field='username', vault='lab_s3') }}"
    40:     routeros_s3_secret_key: "{{ lookup('community.general.onepassword', 'routeros-backups-rustfs-cold', field='password', vault='lab_s3') }}"
    41: 
    42:     routeros_backup_show_sensitive: true
    43:     routeros_backup_binary: true
    44:     routeros_backup_name: "{{ inventory_hostname }}-{{ backup_ts }}"
    45:     # The collection role writes <inventory_hostname>.rsc into this dir; set
    46:     # per-host in pre_tasks to the staging tempdir.
    47:     routeros_backup_dir: "{{ routeros_stage.path }}"

    49:   pre_tasks:
    50:     - name: Compute per-host backup timestamp
    51:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    52:         backup_ts: "{{ lookup('pipe', 'date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ') }}"
    53: 
    54:     - name: Create staging directory on the control node
    55:       ansible.builtin.tempfile:
    56:         state: directory
    57:         prefix: "routeros-backup-{{ inventory_hostname }}-"
    58:       register: routeros_stage
    59:       delegate_to: localhost
    60:       connection: local
    61:       changed_when: false
    62: 
    63:     - name: Tighten staging directory to mode 0700
    64:       ansible.builtin.file:
    65:         path: "{{ routeros_stage.path }}"
    66:         mode: '0700'
    67:       delegate_to: localhost
    68:       connection: local
    69:       changed_when: false
    70: 
    71:   roles:
    72:     - role: david_igou.routeros_configuration.backup
    73: 
    74:   post_tasks:
    75:     # WORKAROUND (remove at collection >= 0.0.8): the backup role's
    76:     # join('\n') emits literal backslash-n under ansible-core >= 2.19, so its
    77:     # .rsc lands as one corrupted line. Rebuild the file from the role's raw
    78:     # export register before uploading. See
    79:     # /tmp/issue-routeros-backup-rsc-literal-newlines.md.
    80:     - name: Rewrite the .rsc from the raw export (collection join('\n') workaround)
    81:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    82:         content: "{{ (_routeros_export.stdout_lines[0] | reject('search', 'by RouterOS') | join(_nl)) ~ _nl }}"
    83:         dest: "{{ routeros_stage.path }}/{{ inventory_hostname }}.rsc"
    84:         mode: "0600"
    85:       vars:
    86:         _nl: "\n"
    87:       delegate_to: localhost
    88:       connection: local
    89: 
    90:     - name: Fetch binary backup off-box (and remove it from device flash)
    91:       ansible.builtin.include_tasks: tasks/fetch_artifact.yml
    92:       vars:
    93:         remote_filename: "{{ routeros_backup_name }}.backup"
    94:         local_dir: "{{ routeros_stage.path }}"
    95: 
    96:     - name: Upload artifacts to S3 with tier tag
    97:       amazon.aws.s3_object:
    98:         endpoint_url: "{{ routeros_s3_endpoint }}"
    99:         access_key: "{{ routeros_s3_access_key }}"
   100:         secret_key: "{{ routeros_s3_secret_key }}"
   101:         region: "{{ routeros_s3_region }}"
   102:         bucket: "{{ routeros_s3_bucket }}"
   103:         object: "{{ routeros_s3_prefix }}/{{ inventory_hostname }}/{{ item.key }}"
   104:         src: "{{ item.src }}"
   105:         mode: put
   106:         tags:
   107:           tier: "{{ routeros_s3_tier }}"
   108:       delegate_to: localhost
   109:       connection: local
   110:       loop:
   111:         - key: "{{ routeros_backup_name }}.backup"
   112:           src: "{{ routeros_stage.path }}/{{ routeros_backup_name }}.backup"
   113:         # The staged .rsc is the role's idempotent <host>.rsc; upload it under
   114:         # the timestamped key so S3 keeps point-in-time history per tier.
   115:         - key: "{{ routeros_backup_name }}.rsc"
   116:           src: "{{ routeros_stage.path }}/{{ inventory_hostname }}.rsc"
   117:       loop_control:
   118:         label: "{{ item.key }}"
   119: 
   120:     - name: Remove staging directory
   121:       ansible.builtin.file:
   122:         path: "{{ routeros_stage.path }}"
   123:         state: absent
   124:       delegate_to: localhost
   125:       connection: local
   126:       changed_when: false

name: ansible/roles/k3s/tasks/os-tuning.yml
review_question: Is this Ansible artifact excessively large and in need of decomposition?
source_context:
1: ---
     2: # roles/k3s/tasks/os-tuning.yml
     3: #
     4: # Persistent OS tuning for Kubernetes (k3s) nodes
     5: #
     6: # Design decisions:
     7: # - inotify limits are enforced via a late /etc/sysctl.d drop-in (99-zzz-*)
     8: #   to avoid Ubuntu/systemd precedence inconsistencies.
     9: # - PAM limits are kept for interactive shells (harmless, optional).
    10: # - systemd DefaultLimitNOFILE is persisted via system.conf.d + daemon-reexec.
    11: # - k3s/containerd/kubelet get explicit LimitNOFILE overrides.
    12: 
    13: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    14: # Inotify limits (authoritative, persistent)
    15: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    16: 
    17: - name: Persist inotify limits via late sysctl.d drop-in
    18:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    19:     dest: /etc/sysctl.d/99-zzz-k3s-inotify.conf
    20:     owner: root
    21:     group: root
    22:     mode: "0644"
    23:     content: |
    24:       fs.inotify.max_user_watches={{ k3s_fs_inotify_max_user_watches }}
    25:       fs.inotify.max_user_instances={{ k3s_fs_inotify_max_user_instances }}
    26:       fs.inotify.max_queued_events={{ k3s_fs_inotify_max_queued_events }}
    27:   become: true
    28:   notify: Reload sysctl
    29: 
    30: - name: Remove legacy inotify sysctl drop-in (avoid conflicts)
    31:   ansible.builtin.file:
    32:     path: /etc/sysctl.d/99-k3s-inotify.conf
    33:     state: absent
    34:   become: true
    35: 
    36: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    37: # Intel GPU perf counters (for OpenVINO stats)
    38: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    39: 
    40: - name: Check for Intel GPU render node vendor
    41:   ansible.builtin.stat:
    42:     path: /sys/class/drm/renderD128/device/vendor
    43:   register: k3s_gpu_vendor_file
    44:   changed_when: false
    45:   become: true
    46: 
    47: - name: Read GPU vendor id
    48:   ansible.builtin.command: cat /sys/class/drm/renderD128/device/vendor
    49:   register: k3s_gpu_vendor_id
    50:   changed_when: false
    51:   when: k3s_gpu_vendor_file.stat.exists | default(false)
    52:   become: true
    53: 
    54: - name: Set Intel GPU detection fact
    55:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    56:     k3s_intel_gpu_present: >-
    57:       {{
    58:         k3s_gpu_vendor_file.stat.exists | default(false)
    59:         and (k3s_gpu_vendor_id.stdout | default('') | trim) == '0x8086'
    60:       }}
    61: 
    62: - name: Persist Intel GPU perf sysctl settings
    63:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    64:     dest: /etc/sysctl.d/99-zzz-k3s-gpu-perf.conf
    65:     owner: root
    66:     group: root
    67:     mode: "0644"
    68:     content: |
    69:       kernel.perf_event_paranoid={{ k3s_perf_event_paranoid }}
    70:       kernel.kptr_restrict={{ k3s_kptr_restrict }}
    71:   become: true
    72:   notify: Reload sysctl
    73:   when:
    74:     - k3s_enable_gpu_perf_sysctl | bool
    75:     - k3s_intel_gpu_present | bool
    76: 
    77: - name: Remove Intel GPU perf sysctl settings when not applicable
    78:   ansible.builtin.file:
    79:     path: /etc/sysctl.d/99-zzz-k3s-gpu-perf.conf
    80:     state: absent
    81:   become: true
    82:   when: not (k3s_enable_gpu_perf_sysctl | bool and k3s_intel_gpu_present | bool)
    83: 
    84: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    85: # File descriptor limits (PAM / interactive shells)
    86: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    87: 
    88: - name: Set nofile limits for interactive sessions (PAM/ssh)
    89:   ansible.builtin.copy:
    90:     dest: /etc/security/limits.d/99-kubernetes.conf
    91:     owner: root
    92:     group: root
    93:     mode: "0644"
    94:     content: |
    95:       * soft nofile {{ k3s_nofile_limit }}
    96:       * hard nofile {{ k3s_nofile_limit }}
    97:   become: true
    98: 
    99: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   100: # systemd defaults (affects services)
   101: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   102: 
   103: - name: Ensure systemd system.conf.d exists
   104:   ansible.builtin.file:
   105:     path: /etc/systemd/system.conf.d
   106:     state: directory
   107:     mode: "0755"
   108:   become: true
   109: 
   110: - name: Persist systemd DefaultLimitNOFILE via drop-in
   111:   ansible.builtin.copy:
   112:     dest: /etc/systemd/system.conf.d/99-k3s-nofile.conf
   113:     mode: "0644"
   114:     content: |
   115:       [Manager]
   116:       DefaultLimitNOFILE={{ k3s_nofile_limit }}
   117:   notify: Re-execute systemd daemon
   118:   become: true
   119: 
   120: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   121: # Per-service overrides (most reliable)
   122: # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   123: 
   124: # containerd (standalone installs)
   125: - name: Check if containerd systemd unit exists
   126:   ansible.builtin.stat:
   127:     path: /lib/systemd/system/containerd.service
   128:   register: k3s_containerd_unit
   129:   become: true
   130: 
   131: - name: Configure containerd service overrides
   132:   when: k3s_containerd_unit.stat.exists
   133:   become: true
   134:   block:
   135:     - name: Ensure containerd override dir exists
   136:       ansible.builtin.file:
   137:         path: /etc/systemd/system/containerd.service.d
   138:         state: directory
   139:         mode: "0755"
   140: 
   141:     - name: Set containerd LimitNOFILE
   142:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   143:         dest: /etc/systemd/system/containerd.service.d/99-nofile.conf
   144:         mode: "0644"
   145:         content: |
   146:           [Service]
   147:           LimitNOFILE={{ k3s_nofile_limit }}
   148:       notify:
   149:         - Reload systemd configuration
   150:         - Restart containerd
   151: 
   152: # k3s (single-binary service; embedded containerd)
   153: - name: Check if k3s systemd unit exists
   154:   ansible.builtin.stat:
   155:     path: /lib/systemd/system/k3s.service
   156:   register: k3s_unit
   157:   become: true
   158: 
   159: - name: Configure k3s service overrides
   160:   when: k3s_unit.stat.exists
   161:   become: true
   162:   block:
   163:     - name: Ensure k3s override dir exists
   164:       ansible.builtin.file:
   165:         path: /etc/systemd/system/k3s.service.d
   166:         state: directory
   167:         mode: "0755"
   168: 
   169:     - name: Set k3s LimitNOFILE
   170:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   171:         dest: /etc/systemd/system/k3s.service.d/99-nofile.conf
   172:         mode: "0644"
   173:         content: |
   174:           [Service]
   175:           LimitNOFILE={{ k3s_nofile_limit }}
   176:       notify:
   177:         - Reload systemd configuration
   178:         - Restart k3s
   179: 
   180: # kubelet (only if present; safe no-op on pure k3s)
   181: - name: Check if kubelet systemd unit exists
   182:   ansible.builtin.stat:
   183:     path: /lib/systemd/system/kubelet.service
   184:   register: k3s_kubelet_unit
   185:   become: true
   186: 
   187: - name: Configure kubelet service overrides
   188:   when: k3s_kubelet_unit.stat.exists
   189:   become: true
   190:   block:
   191:     - name: Ensure kubelet override dir exists
   192:       ansible.builtin.file:
   193:         path: /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d
   194:         state: directory
   195:         mode: "0755"
   196: 
   197:     - name: Set kubelet LimitNOFILE
   198:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   199:         dest: /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/99-nofile.conf
   200:         mode: "0644"
   201:         content: |
   202:           [Service]
   203:           LimitNOFILE={{ k3s_nofile_limit }}
   204:       notify:
   205:         - Reload systemd configuration
   206:         - Restart kubelet

source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Gateway collector — OpenTelemetry-recommended "gateway pattern" implementation.
     3: # Called from setup.yml when `opentelemetry_gateway_enabled: true`, *before*
     4: # the helm task so the gateway collector spec AND its supporting resources
     5: # (htpasswd Secret + Ingress) are included in the chart values.
     6: #
     7: # All resources go through helm via:
     8: #   - `collectors.<gateway_name>` (the OpenTelemetryCollector CR + the
     9: #     operator-spawned Service/Deployment) → driven by
    10: #     `opentelemetry_collectors[<gateway_name>]`
    11: #   - `extraObjects[]` (Secret + Ingress) → driven by
    12: #     `opentelemetry_additional_config.extraObjects`
    13: #
    14: # That way helm owns the full lifecycle: a `helm upgrade` after disabling
    15: # the gateway tears everything down, and credential rotation is reflected
    16: # through a pod-annotation checksum so the operator triggers a rollout.
    17: 
    18: - name: "Compute gateway derived values"
    19:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    20:     _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name: "{{ opentelemetry_release_name }}-{{ opentelemetry_gateway_name }}"
    21:     _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name: "{{ opentelemetry_release_name }}-{{ opentelemetry_gateway_name }}-htpasswd"
    22:     _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled: "{{ (opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd | default('') | length) > 0 }}"
    23: 
    24: - name: "Build the gateway collector spec"
    25:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    26:     opentelemetry_collectors: >-
    27:       {{
    28:         (opentelemetry_collectors | default({}))
    29:         | combine({ opentelemetry_gateway_name: _opentelemetry_gateway_collector_spec }, recursive=True)
    30:       }}
    31:   vars:
    32:     _volumes: >-
    33:       {{
    34:         [{
    35:           'name': 'htpasswd',
    36:           'secret': {'secretName': _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name}
    37:         }]
    38:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    39:       }}
    40:     _volume_mounts: >-
    41:       {{
    42:         [{
    43:           'name': 'htpasswd',
    44:           'mountPath': '/etc/otel-auth',
    45:           'readOnly': true
    46:         }]
    47:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    48:       }}
    49:     # Credential rotation: the basicauth/server extension caches the
    50:     # htpasswd file at startup, so secret content changes only take effect
    51:     # when the pod restarts. Putting a checksum of the content in
    52:     # podAnnotations makes the operator roll the pod whenever the content
    53:     # differs from the previous apply.
    54:     _pod_annotations: >-
    55:       {{
    56:         {'checksum/htpasswd': (opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd | hash('sha256'))}
    57:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else {}
    58:       }}
    59:     _extensions: >-
    60:       {{
    61:         {'basicauth/server': {'htpasswd': {'file': '/etc/otel-auth/htpasswd'}}}
    62:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else {}
    63:       }}
    64:     _service_extensions: >-
    65:       {{
    66:         ['basicauth/server']
    67:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled else []
    68:       }}
    69:     # Auto-wire basicauth/server onto the OTLP HTTP receiver. We deep-merge
    70:     # so the user keeps full control of receiver options (compression,
    71:     # max_recv_msg_size, …).
    72:     _otlp_http_auth_overlay:
    73:       otlp:
    74:         protocols:
    75:           http:
    76:             auth:
    77:               authenticator: "basicauth/server"
    78:     _receivers: >-
    79:       {{
    80:         opentelemetry_gateway_receivers
    81:         | combine(_otlp_http_auth_overlay, recursive=True)
    82:         if _opentelemetry_gateway_auth_enabled
    83:         else opentelemetry_gateway_receivers
    84:       }}
    85:     # If the user did not provide explicit pipelines, route every receiver +
    86:     # processor + exporter into metrics & logs pipelines. Works for the
    87:     # common case of homogeneous OTLP exporters; override when you have
    88:     # signal-specific routing.
    89:     _default_pipelines:
    90:       metrics:
    91:         receivers: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_receivers.keys() | list }}"
    92:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors.keys() | list }}"
    93:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters.keys() | list }}"
    94:       logs:
    95:         receivers: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_receivers.keys() | list }}"
    96:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors.keys() | list }}"
    97:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters.keys() | list }}"
    98:     _pipelines: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_pipelines if (opentelemetry_gateway_pipelines | length > 0) else _default_pipelines }}"
    99:     _opentelemetry_gateway_collector_spec:
   100:       enabled: true
   101:       mode: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_mode }}"
   102:       replicas: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_replicas }}"
   103:       # Predictable service name (`<release>-<gateway_name>-collector`),
   104:       # otherwise the chart defaults to `<release>-collector` which
   105:       # collides with any other non-daemon collector. Required for the
   106:       # Ingress backend reference below.
   107:       fullnameOverride: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name }}"
   108:       resources: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_resources }}"
   109:       volumes: "{{ _volumes }}"
   110:       volumeMounts: "{{ _volume_mounts }}"
   111:       podAnnotations: "{{ _pod_annotations }}"
   112:       config:
   113:         extensions: "{{ _extensions }}"
   114:         receivers: "{{ _receivers }}"
   115:         processors: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_processors }}"
   116:         exporters: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_exporters }}"
   117:         service:
   118:           extensions: "{{ _service_extensions }}"
   119:           pipelines: "{{ _pipelines }}"
   120: 
   121: - name: "Inject the gateway Secret + Ingress as chart extraObjects"
   122:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   123:     opentelemetry_additional_config: >-
   124:       {{
   125:         (opentelemetry_additional_config | default({}))
   126:         | combine({
   127:             'extraObjects': (
   128:               ((opentelemetry_additional_config | default({})).extraObjects | default([]))
   129:               + _gateway_extra_objects
   130:             )
   131:           })
   132:       }}
   133:   when: _gateway_extra_objects | length > 0
   134:   vars:
   135:     _htpasswd_secret_obj:
   136:       apiVersion: "v1"
   137:       kind: "Secret"
   138:       metadata:
   139:         name: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd_secret_name }}"
   140:         namespace: "{{ opentelemetry_namespace }}"
   141:       type: "Opaque"
   142:       stringData:
   143:         htpasswd: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_htpasswd }}"
   144:     _ingress_obj:
   145:       apiVersion: "networking.k8s.io/v1"
   146:       kind: "Ingress"
   147:       metadata:
   148:         name: "{{ _opentelemetry_gateway_full_name }}"
   149:         namespace: "{{ opentelemetry_namespace }}"
   150:         annotations: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_annotations }}"
   151:       spec:
   152:         ingressClassName: "{{ opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_class_name }}"
   153:         tls: >-
   154:           {{
   155:             [{
   156:               'hosts': [opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_hostname],
   157:               'secretName': opentelemetry_gateway_ingress_tls_secret_name
   158:             }]
