source_context:
1: ---
     2: # Reusable pair-handshake task file (issue #437, locked-pair fix #445).
     3: #
     4: # Every lifecycle op that brings the zeroclaw daemon up MUST include this
     5: # file. There is no skip path.
     6: #
     7: # Two-branch state machine, picked off the /pair/code response shape:
     8: #
     9: #   1. Fresh daemon (no row in devices.db) -> GET /pair/code returns a
    10: #      non-null pairing_code. Use it directly.
    11: #   2. Locked daemon (devices.db has prior rows, survives systemctl
    12: #      restart) -> GET /pair/code returns {"pairing_code": null}. POST
    13: #      to /api/pairing/initiate with the existing bearer to mint a fresh
    14: #      code, then continue down the same POST /pair path.
    15: #
    16: # Both branches converge on the existing X-Pairing-Code exchange.
    17: #
    18: # Inputs:
    19: #   - gateway_local_base: http://127.0.0.1:<port> (set by including playbook)
    20: #   - ansible_host, gateway_port (used to emit zeroclaw_gateway_url fact)
    21: #   - agent_name, agent_type (used in failure messages)
    22: #   - config.gateway.auth: current Bearer from hosts.json. Required only
    23: #     when /pair/code returns null. May be empty/undefined on first install
    24: #     (when the locked branch cannot fire anyway).
    25: #
    26: # Outputs (cacheable host facts; configure_agent / restart_agent read these
    27: # out of artifacts/<run>/fact_cache):
    28: #   - zeroclaw_gateway_token: bearer token minted by /pair
    29: #   - zeroclaw_gateway_url:   ws://<host>:<port>/ws/chat
    30: 
    31: - name: Request pairing code (fresh-boot branch)
    32:   ansible.builtin.uri:
    33:     url: "{{ gateway_local_base }}/pair/code"
    34:     method: GET
    35:     status_code: 200
    36:     timeout: 10
    37:     return_content: yes
    38:   register: pair_code_response
    39:   no_log: true
    40: 
    41: # Locked branch: zeroclaw v0.7.5's /pair/code returns
    42: # {"pairing_code": null, "pairing_required": true} once devices.db has any
    43: # prior row. The authenticated initiate endpoint mints a fresh code that
    44: # the existing POST /pair task below can consume unchanged.
    45: #
    46: # ATX B2: explicitly accept 401 and 503 so the recovery path produces an
    47: # actionable operator message instead of a raw `Status code was 401`
    48: # Ansible error. The `Validate locked-branch initiate response` task below
    49: # then fails with explicit guidance to re-run `clawctl agent configure` (401)
    50: # or check daemon health (503).
    51: - name: Mint pairing code via /api/pairing/initiate (locked-pair branch)
    52:   ansible.builtin.uri:
    53:     url: "{{ gateway_local_base }}/api/pairing/initiate"
    54:     method: POST
    55:     status_code: [200, 401, 503]
    56:     timeout: 10
    57:     headers:
    58:       Authorization: "Bearer {{ config.gateway.auth | default('') }}"
    59:     return_content: yes
    60:   register: initiate_response
    61:   no_log: true
    62:   when:
    63:     - pair_code_response.json is defined
    64:     - pair_code_response.json.pairing_code is none
    65: 
    66: # ATX B2: surface 401/503 as actionable operator messages BEFORE the
    67: # resolved_pairing_code set_fact runs, so the operator sees the right
    68: # remediation instead of a generic "pairing code" failure downstream.
    69: #
    70: # ATX iter-3 NB2: this task MUST NOT carry `no_log: true`. The
    71: # lifecycle.py censored-event handler (W1) skips events where
    72: # `res.censored` is set, which silently swallows the operator-actionable
    73: # branching this msg encodes. The current msg references only
    74: # `initiate_response.status` (an int — safe to log) plus the constants
    75: # `agent_name` and `agent_type`. Future editors:
    76: #
    77: #   WARNING: do NOT reference `initiate_response.json` or
    78: #   `initiate_response.content` in this msg. A debug-mode daemon may echo
    79: #   the Authorization header back in its 401 body; templating that into
    80: #   the msg would leak the bearer through the fail-msg path that bypasses
    81: #   no_log.
    82: - name: Validate locked-branch initiate response
    83:   ansible.builtin.fail:
    84:     msg: >-
    85:       {% if initiate_response.status == 401 %}POST /api/pairing/initiate
    86:       returned 401: the bearer in hosts.json is stale (likely because
    87:       devices.db was wiped or rebuilt on the host). Run
    88:       `clawctl agent configure {{ agent_name }}` to re-pair from scratch.
    89:       {% elif initiate_response.status == 503 %}POST /api/pairing/initiate
    90:       returned 503: zeroclaw daemon reports pairing disabled or unavailable.
    91:       Check `journalctl --unit {{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}` and restart
    92:       the daemon, then re-run `clawctl agent configure {{ agent_name }}`.
    93:       {% else %}POST /api/pairing/initiate returned an unexpected status
    94:       {{ initiate_response.status }} — see daemon logs.
    95:       {% endif %}
    96:   when:
    97:     - initiate_response is defined
    98:     - initiate_response.status is defined
    99:     - initiate_response.status != 200
   100: 
   101: - name: Resolve pairing code from whichever branch produced one
   102:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   103:     resolved_pairing_code: >-
   104:       {{
   105:         (initiate_response.json.pairing_code
   106:           if (pair_code_response.json is defined
   107:               and pair_code_response.json.pairing_code is none
   108:               and initiate_response is defined
   109:               and initiate_response.json is defined)
   110:           else pair_code_response.json.pairing_code)
   111:         if pair_code_response.json is defined else none
   112:       }}
   113:   no_log: true
   114: 
   115: # Do NOT set `no_log: true` on this fail task. The msg body is pure
   116: # template-literal text (`agent_name`, `agent_type` — both safe to log).
   117: - name: Validate pairing code shape
   118:   ansible.builtin.fail:
   119:     msg: >-
   120:       Neither GET /pair/code nor POST /api/pairing/initiate returned a usable
   121:       pairing code. Check daemon logs:
   122:       `journalctl --unit {{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}`. If devices.db was
   123:       wiped externally, run `clawctl agent configure {{ agent_name }}` after
   124:       restoring it.
   125:   when:
   126:     - resolved_pairing_code is not defined
   127:       or resolved_pairing_code is none
   128:       or resolved_pairing_code | length < 1
   129: 
   130: # ATX W2: declared format guard for the pairing code before it enters the
   131: # X-Pairing-Code HTTP header. Python's http.client already rejects CRLF in
   132: # header values since 3.4, so this is preventative rather than load-bearing;
   133: # the regex also documents the contract (alphanumeric/_/- max 128 chars) so
   134: # a future caller can't silently reuse the value in a shell command or URL
   135: # path without re-validating.
   136: - name: Validate pairing code format
   137:   ansible.builtin.fail:
   138:     msg: >-
   139:       Pairing code returned by the daemon has an unexpected format. Daemon
   140:       logs: `journalctl --unit {{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}`.
   141:   when:
   142:     - resolved_pairing_code is not match('^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$')
   143: 
   144: # ZeroClaw v0.7.5 expects the one-time code via the `X-Pairing-Code` HTTP
   145: # header (per the daemon's startup banner), not a JSON body.
   146: - name: Exchange pairing code for bearer token
   147:   ansible.builtin.uri:
   148:     url: "{{ gateway_local_base }}/pair"
   149:     method: POST
   150:     status_code: 200
   151:     timeout: 10
   152:     headers:
   153:       X-Pairing-Code: "{{ resolved_pairing_code }}"
   154:     return_content: yes
   155:   register: pair_response
   156:   no_log: true
   157: 
   158: - name: Validate bearer token shape
   159:   ansible.builtin.fail:
   160:     msg: >-
   161:       /pair did not return a usable token. Daemon logs:
   162:       `journalctl --unit {{ agent_type }}-{{ agent_name }}`. Re-run
   163:       `clawctl agent configure {{ agent_name }}` after fixing the daemon.
   164:   when:
   165:     - pair_response.json is not defined
   166:       or pair_response.json.token is not defined
   167:       or pair_response.json.token is none
   168:       or pair_response.json.token | length < 16
   169: 
   170: # Emit gateway token + URL as cacheable host facts. The Python caller reads
   171: # them out of artifacts/<run>/fact_cache and persists them to hosts.json
   172: # under agents.<n>.config.gateway.{auth,url}. Mirrors the OpenClaw
   173: # fact-emission pattern in install.py:307-316. `no_log: true` so the value
   174: # isn't echoed at -vvv.
   175: - name: Save gateway credentials as cacheable facts
   176:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   177:     zeroclaw_gateway_token: "{{ pair_response.json.token }}"
   178:     zeroclaw_gateway_url: "ws://{{ ansible_host }}:{{ gateway_port }}/ws/chat"
   179:     cacheable: true
   180:   no_log: true

   165: # === adding monitor on other nodes ===
   166: - name: Add hosts to Ceph orchestrator with _admin label
   167:   ansible.builtin.command: "ceph orch host add {{ hostvars[item]['hostname'] }} --labels _admin"

   185:   when: cephadm_mon_nodes_to_add | length > 0
   186: 
   187: # === OSDs now ===
   188: # A volume is kept untouched if and only if it hosts an OSD that the
   189: # running cluster claims: the OSD uuid found in the LVM tags written by
   190: # ceph-volume must be registered in the cluster OSD map. Everything else
   191: # listed as an OSD volume belongs to Ceph and is zapped before being
   192: # added, which makes re-runs safe on live clusters and makes
   193: # reinstallations and machine replacements re-enroll leftover volumes
   194: # automatically.
   195: - name: Set OSD volume candidates for this host
   196:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   197:     cephadm_osd_disks: >-
   198:       {{ ceph_osd_disks
   199:          if ceph_osd_disks is defined
   200:          else ([ceph_osd_disk] if ceph_osd_disk is defined else []) }}
   201: 
   202: - name: Get the OSD map of the cluster
   203:   ansible.builtin.command: ceph osd dump --format json
   204:   register: cephadm_osd_dump
   205:   changed_when: false
   206:   run_once: true
   207:   delegate_to: "{{ cephadm_first_node }}"
   208: 
   209: - name: Set fact for OSD UUIDs registered in the cluster
   210:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   211:     cephadm_cluster_osd_uuids: "{{ (cephadm_osd_dump.stdout | from_json).osds | map(attribute='uuid') | list }}"
   212:   run_once: true
   213: 
   214: - name: List ceph-volume OSDs of the host
   215:   ansible.builtin.command: "{{ cephadm_bin }} --image localhost:5000/ceph:v{{ cephadm_release }} ceph-volume lvm list --format json"
   216:   register: cephadm_cv_list
   217:   changed_when: false
   218:   failed_when: false
   219:   when: cephadm_osd_disks | default([]) | length > 0
   220: 
   221: - name: Compute devices claimed by OSDs of the cluster
   222:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   223:     cephadm_claimed_devices: "{{ cephadm_osd_lvs | community.general.json_query(cephadm_claimed_query) | flatten }}"
   224:   vars:
   225:     cephadm_osd_lvs: >-
   226:       {{ ((cephadm_cv_list.stdout | default('{}'))
   227:           if (cephadm_cv_list.rc | default(1)) == 0 else '{}')
   228:          | from_json | dict2items | map(attribute='value') | flatten | list }}
   229:     cephadm_claimed_query: >-
   230:       [?contains(`{{ cephadm_cluster_osd_uuids | to_json }}`, tags."ceph.osd_fsid")].[lv_path, devices]
   231:   when: cephadm_osd_disks | default([]) | length > 0
   232: 
   233: - name: Get the real path of OSD volumes
   234:   ansible.builtin.command: "realpath {{ item }}"
   235:   loop: "{{ cephadm_osd_disks | default([]) }}"
   236:   register: cephadm_osd_disks_realpath
   237:   changed_when: false
   238:   failed_when: false
   239: 
   240: - name: List the block device tree of each OSD volume
   241:   ansible.builtin.command: "lsblk -lnpo NAME {{ item.stdout }}"
   242:   loop: "{{ cephadm_osd_disks_realpath.results | default([]) }}"
   243:   loop_control:
   244:     label: "{{ item.item | default('') }}"
   245:   register: cephadm_osd_disks_tree
   246:   changed_when: false
   247:   when: item.rc | default(1) == 0
   248: 
   249: - name: Select OSD volumes not claimed by the cluster
   250:   ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   251:     cephadm_osd_disks_to_zap: >-
   252:       {{ cephadm_osd_disks_to_zap | default([])
   253:          + ([item.item.item] if (item.rc | default(1)) == 0
   254:             and item.item.item not in cephadm_claimed_devices
   255:             and item.stdout_lines | intersect(cephadm_claimed_devices) | length == 0
   256:             else []) }}
   257:   loop: "{{ cephadm_osd_disks_tree.results | default([]) }}"
   258:   loop_control:
   259:     label: "{{ item.item.item | default('') }}"
   260: 
   261: - name: Show OSD volumes that will be wiped
   262:   ansible.builtin.debug:
   263:     msg: "OSD volumes that will be wiped and given to Ceph: {{ cephadm_osd_disks_to_zap | default([]) }}"
   264:   when: cephadm_osd_disks_to_zap | default([]) | length > 0
   265: 
   266: # Logical volumes are wiped in place (the volume belongs to the user);
   267: # whole disks and partitions are destroyed so that ceph-volume can
   268: # create its own LVM layer on them.
   269: - name: Get the device type of OSD volumes to wipe
   270:   ansible.builtin.command: "lsblk -ndo TYPE {{ item }}"
   271:   loop: "{{ cephadm_osd_disks_to_zap | default([]) }}"
   272:   register: cephadm_osd_zap_types
   273:   changed_when: false
   274: 
   275: - name: Zap OSD volumes not claimed by the cluster
   276:   ansible.builtin.command: >-
   277:     {{ cephadm_bin }} --image localhost:5000/ceph:v{{ cephadm_release }}
   278:     ceph-volume lvm zap {{ item.item }}{{ '' if (item.stdout | trim) == 'lvm' else ' --destroy' }}
   279:   loop: "{{ cephadm_osd_zap_types.results | default([]) }}"
   280:   loop_control:
   281:     label: "{{ item.item }}"
   282:   changed_when: true
   283: 
   284: - name: Copy ceph orch spec file
   285:   ansible.builtin.template:
   286:     src: "{{ cephadm_spec_path | default('spec.yaml.j2') }}"
   287:     dest: /tmp/t.yaml
   288:     mode: "0644"
   289:   run_once: true
   290:   delegate_to: "{{ cephadm_first_node }}"
   291: 
   292: - name: Add OSD daemon on nodes that need OSDs
   293:   ansible.builtin.command: "{{ cephadm_bin }} --image localhost:5000/ceph:v{{ cephadm_release }} shell -v /tmp/t.yaml:/tmp/t.yaml:ro -- ceph orch apply -i /tmp/t.yaml"
   294:   delegate_to: "{{ cephadm_first_node }}"
   295:   run_once: true
   296:   changed_when: true
   297:   failed_when: false
   298: 
   299: - name: Confirm cluster is ok
   300:   ansible.builtin.command: ceph status --format=json
   301:   register: cephadm_cephs
   302:   retries: 30
   303:   delay: 10
   304:   changed_when: false
   305:   run_once: true
   306:   delegate_to: "{{ cephadm_first_node }}"
   307:   until: cephadm_cephs.stdout | from_json | community.general.json_query('health.status') == "HEALTH_OK"
   308: 
   309: - name: Check if RBD pool exists
   310:   ansible.builtin.shell:
   311:     cmd: set -o pipefail && ceph osd lspools | grep -w rbd
   312:     executable: /bin/bash
   313:   register: cephadm_rbd_pool_check
   314:   changed_when: false
   315:   failed_when: false
   316: 
   317: - name: Create RBD pool if it doesn't exist
   318:   ansible.builtin.command: ceph osd pool create rbd
   319:   when: cephadm_rbd_pool_check.rc != 0
   320:   changed_when: true
   321:   run_once: true
   322:   delegate_to: "{{ cephadm_first_node }}"
   323: 
   324: - name: Enable RBD application on the pool
   325:   ansible.builtin.command: ceph osd pool application enable rbd rbd
   326:   when: cephadm_rbd_pool_check.rc != 0
   327:   changed_when: true
   328:   run_once: true
   329:   delegate_to: "{{ cephadm_first_node }}"
   330: 
   331: - name: Check if CephX user client.libvirt exists
   332:   ansible.builtin.command: ceph auth get client.libvirt
   333:   register: cephadm_cephx_user_check
   334:   changed_when: false
   335:   failed_when: false
   336: 
   337: - name: Create CephX user client.libvirt if it does not exist
   338:   ansible.builtin.command: >
   339:     ceph auth add client.libvirt
   340:     mon 'profile rbd, allow command "osd blacklist"'
   341:     osd 'allow class-read object_prefix rbd_children, profile rbd pool=rbd'
   342:   when: cephadm_cephx_user_check.rc != 0
   343:   changed_when: true

   349:     osd 'allow class-read object_prefix rbd_children, profile rbd pool=rbd'
   350:   when: cephadm_cephx_user_check.rc == 0
   351:   changed_when: true

   355:     name: registry
   356:     state: absent

     7: # Not /etc/logrotate.d: these configs name /var/log/syslog and /var/log/kern.log,
     8: # which the distro's own rsyslog config already covers. logrotate refuses a
     9: # duplicate log entry and aborts the whole run with "found error in file rsyslog,
    10: # skipping", so the daily logrotate.service fails and nothing under
    11: # /etc/logrotate.d gets rotated. They are driven by /etc/cron.d/logrotate-bloom
    12: # with an explicit path, so a directory outside the include is enough.
    13: - name: Create bloom logrotate directory
    14:   file:
    15:     path: /etc/logrotate-bloom.d
    16:     state: directory
    17:     mode: "0755"
    18: 
    19: - name: Create iSCSI aggressive logrotate config
    20:   copy:
    21:     content: |
    22:       # /etc/logrotate-bloom.d/iscsi-aggressive.conf
    23:       /var/log/kern.log
    24:       /var/log/syslog
    25:       {
    26:           # /var/log is root:syslog 775, which logrotate refuses to rotate into
    27:           # unless it is told whom to become. /etc/logrotate.conf carries the
    28:           # same "su root adm", but the cron job runs logrotate against this
    29:           # file alone and so never reads it: without this line every run ends
    30:           # in "skipping ... because parent directory has insecure permissions"
    31:           # and syslog is never rotated at all.
    32:           su root adm
    33:           size 200M
    34:           rotate 10
    35:           compress
    36:           delaycompress
    37:           missingok
    38:           notifempty
    39:           create 0640 syslog adm
    40:           # No dateext. A size condition rotates more than once a day on a
    41:           # busy node, and dateext names every archive after the day alone,
    42:           # so the second rotation of a day collides with the first and is
    43:           # skipped. The numbered suffix has no such limit and it is what
    44:           # the distribution uses for every other log here.
    45:           postrotate
    46:               /usr/lib/rsyslog/rsyslog-rotate
    47:           endscript
    48:       }
    49:     dest: /etc/logrotate-bloom.d/iscsi-aggressive.conf
    50:     mode: "0644"
    51: 
    52: - name: Create RKE2 logrotate config
    53:   copy:
    54:     content: |
    55:       /var/lib/rancher/rke2/agent/containerd/containerd.log
    56:       {
    57:           size 100M
    58:           rotate 5
    59:           compress
    60:           delaycompress
    61:           missingok
    62:           notifempty
    63:           create 0640 root root
    64:           # No dateext, for the reason given on the iSCSI config above.
    65:       }
    66:     dest: /etc/logrotate-bloom.d/rke2.conf
    67:     mode: "0644"
    68: 
    69: # The extensionless names are from the first version of this task, which was
    70: # documented as "sudo cp ... /etc/logrotate.d/iscsi-aggressive". A later
    71: # version switched to a .conf suffix without removing them, so int-test still
    72: # carries both plus an .bak, and each one duplicates the same two log paths.
    73: # One stale copy is enough to abort the whole logrotate run, so remove every
    74: # name this task has ever written.
    75: - name: Remove logrotate configs written by earlier bloom versions
    76:   file:
    77:     path: "/etc/logrotate.d/{{ item }}"
    78:     state: absent
    79:   loop:
    80:     - iscsi-aggressive.conf
    81:     - iscsi-aggressive
    82:     - iscsi-aggressive.bak
    83:     - rke2.conf
    84:     - rke2
    85: 
    86: # Neither job runs on minute 0, and no two of them share a minute. Both use
    87: # logrotate's default state file /var/lib/logrotate/status, and logrotate
    88: # takes an exclusive lock on it: a second logrotate that starts while the
    89: # first still holds the lock exits with "error: state file
    90: # /var/lib/logrotate/status is already locked". Three runs used to meet on
    91: # minute 0, the two below plus the distribution logrotate.service, which
    92: # logrotate.timer starts at 00:00. The error is collected in
    93: # /var/log/logrotate-bloom.log.
    94: #
    95: # No -f on either command. -f forces the rotation whatever the config says,
    96: # so "size 200M" and "size 100M" below never applied: every run rotated, and
    97: # with the dateext the configs used to carry, only the first run of a day
    98: # could, the rest ending in "destination /var/log/syslog-<date> already
    99: # exists, skipping rotation". Without -f logrotate rotates when the file
   100: # passes the size, which is what the two configs were written for.
   101: #
   102: # Offsets rather than a state file for each job: the iSCSI config and the
   103: # distribution rsyslog config both name /var/log/syslog and /var/log/kern.log,
   104: # and the one shared state file is what stops the size rotation here and the
   105: # weekly rotation there from rotating the same file twice.
   106: - name: Create logrotate cron job
   107:   copy:
   108:     content: |
   109:       # Managed by Ansible - cluster-bloom
   110:       SHELL=/bin/sh
   111:       PATH=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/sbin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin
   112: 
   113:       # iSCSI logrotate - runs every 10 minutes, on minutes 1 to 51
   114:       1,11,21,31,41,51 * * * * root /usr/sbin/logrotate /etc/logrotate-bloom.d/iscsi-aggressive.conf >> /var/log/logrotate-bloom.log 2>&1
   115: 
   116:       # logrotate for RKE2 logs - runs hourly, on minute 5
   117:       5 * * * * root /usr/sbin/logrotate /etc/logrotate-bloom.d/rke2.conf >> /var/log/logrotate-bloom.log 2>&1
   118:     dest: /etc/cron.d/logrotate-bloom
   119:     mode: "0644"
   120: 
   121: - name: Configure rsyslog rate limiting
   122:   block:
   123:     # No module(load="imuxsock" ...) here: /etc/rsyslog.conf already loads
   124:     # imuxsock, a second load is rejected with "module 'imuxsock' already in
   125:     # this config", and the parameter was spelled SysSockRateLimit.Interval
   126:     # rather than SysSock.RateLimit.Interval, so it never applied either.
   127:     #
   128:     # No dynaFile="default" on the action: omfile takes file or dynaFile, not
   129:     # both, and no template named 'default' exists, so rsyslog disabled the
   130:     # action and the rate limit never took effect.
   131:     - name: Create rsyslog iSCSI filter
   132:       copy:
   133:         content: |
   134:           # /etc/rsyslog.d/01-iscsi-filter.conf
   135:           ruleset(name="iscsi_ratelimit") {
   136:               if ($msg contains "detected conn error") or
   137:               ($msg contains "session recovery timed out") or
   138:               ($msg contains "longhorn") then {
   139:                   action(type="omfile"
   140:                       file="/var/log/syslog"
   141:                       action.execOnlyEveryNthTime="500"
   142:                       action.execOnlyEveryNthTimeTimeout="1200"
   143:                   )
   144:                   stop
   145:               }
   146:           }
   147:         dest: /etc/rsyslog.d/01-iscsi-filter.conf
   148:         mode: "0644"
   149:       notify: Restart rsyslog
   150:   tags: [logging, deploy_cluster]
   151: 
   152: - name: Ensure cron is running
   153:   service:
   154:     name: cron
   155:     state: started
   156:     enabled: yes

     8: - name: Generate ephemeral SSL passphrase
     9:   command: >
    10:     python3 -c
    11:     "import secrets, base64; print(base64.b64encode(secrets.token_bytes(40)).decode())"
    12:   register: ssl_passphrase
    13:   changed_when: false
    14:   no_log: true
    15: 
    16: - name: Ensure Splunk auth directory exists

    18:     path: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/auth"

    22:     mode: '0700'

    24:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"

    26: - name: Write cert bundle script
    27:   copy:
    28:     dest: /tmp/splunk_bundle_cert.py
    29:     content: |
    30:       from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import (
    31:           load_pem_private_key, Encoding, PrivateFormat, BestAvailableEncryption
    32:       )
    33:       import sys
    34: 
    35:       passphrase = sys.argv[1].encode()
    36:       key_path   = '/mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/tls.key'
    37:       cert_path  = '/mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/tls.crt'
    38:       out_path   = sys.argv[2] + '/etc/auth/splunk-server-bundle.pem'
    39: 
    40:       with open(key_path, 'rb') as f:
    41:           key = load_pem_private_key(f.read(), password=None)
    42: 
    43:       enc_key_pem = key.private_bytes(
    44:           Encoding.PEM,
    45:           PrivateFormat.PKCS8,
    46:           BestAvailableEncryption(passphrase)
    47:       )
    48: 
    49:       with open(cert_path, 'rb') as f:
    50:           cert_pem = f.read()
    51: 
    52:       with open(out_path, 'wb') as f:
    53:           f.write(cert_pem)

    71:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"

    73:   become: yes
    74:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"

    90:       # tls.crt from the operator-mounted secret may contain intermediate
    91:       # certs that are not repeated in ca.crt (e.g. Vault PKI issuers put
    92:       # only the root in ca.crt). Splunk requires the full chain to be
    93:       # present locally in sslRootCAPath -- it does not complete the chain
    94:       # using intermediates presented by the peer during the handshake.
    95:       # Assemble tls.crt's non-leaf certs + ca.crt into one deduplicated
    96:       # trust bundle.
    97:       import sys
    98: 
    99:       tls_crt_path = '/mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/tls.crt'
   100:       ca_crt_path = '/mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/ca.crt'
   101:       out_path = sys.argv[1] + '/etc/auth/splunk-server-ca.pem'
   102: 
   103:       def split_pem_certs(data):
   104:           certs = []
   105:           current = []
   106:           for line in data.splitlines(keepends=True):
   107:               if line.strip() == b'-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----':
   108:                   current = [line]
   109:               elif line.strip() == b'-----END CERTIFICATE-----':
   110:                   current.append(line)
   111:                   certs.append(b''.join(current))
   112:                   current = []
   113:               elif current:
   114:                   current.append(line)
   115:           return certs
   116: 
   117:       with open(tls_crt_path, 'rb') as f:
   118:           tls_certs = split_pem_certs(f.read())
   119:       chain_certs = tls_certs[1:]  # drop the leaf; keep any presented intermediates/root
   120: 
   121:       with open(ca_crt_path, 'rb') as f:
   122:           ca_certs = split_pem_certs(f.read())
   123: 
   124:       seen = set()
   125:       ordered = []
   126:       for cert in chain_certs + ca_certs:
   127:           if cert not in seen:
   128:               seen.add(cert)
   129:               ordered.append(cert)
   130: 
   131:       with open(out_path, 'wb') as f:
   132:           for cert in ordered:
   133:               f.write(cert)
   134:               if not cert.endswith(b'\n'):
   135:                   f.write(b'\n')
   136:     mode: '0700'

   145:   changed_when: true
